AT.note: Austria pays a lot of cash to families: universal child benefit, a €2,000-per-child tax credit and a well-paid, flexible parental-leave allowance (up to 80% of net pay for about a year). The weak spot is childcare: there is no legal entitlement to a place, only about one in three under-3s has one, and outside Vienna, Burgenland and Carinthia full-day kindergarten costs money. All cash benefits are frozen at 2025 levels for 2026 and 2027 (indexation suspended), so they lose value against inflation.

headline.cash: ≈ €445/month for 2 small kids (Familienbeihilfe + Kinderabsetzbetrag, 2026)
headline.leave: ≈ 12–14 months Kinderbetreuungsgeld at 80% of net pay (max ≈ €2,400/month); 1 paid Papamonat
headline.childcare: no legal entitlement; free all-day kindergarten in Vienna, free half-day mandatory year from 5 nationwide
headline.tax: Familienbonus Plus €2,000/child/year off income tax (≈ €333/month for 2 kids)

policies.name: Kinderbetreuungsgeld (income-dependent variant) + Partnerschaftsbonus
policies.what: Parental-leave allowance chosen per child. Income-dependent variant: 80% of previous net earnings, max €80.12/day (≈ €2,400/month, 2026), for 365 days if one parent takes it, 426 days if both (61 days reserved for the second parent). Flat-rate 'Konto' alternative: €41.14/day for 365 days down to €17.65/day for 851 days. €500 bonus each if split roughly 50/50.
policies.value: ≈ €2,000/month for ~12 months per child at median net pay (≈ €24,000 per child); job protected up to the child's 2nd birthday
policies.eligibility: Parent in insured employment for 182 days before birth; parent must be on leave; earnings cap €8,600/year while receiving it.
policies.caveat: Daily rates frozen at 2025 level for 2026 and 2027 (indexation suspended). The reserved 61 days for the second parent are lost if not used; in practice most fathers take little.

policies.name: Familienbeihilfe + Kinderabsetzbetrag
policies.what: Universal monthly child benefit, no income test: €138.40 per child under 3, €148.00 age 3–9, €171.80 age 10–18 (2026), plus €8.60 per child sibling supplement for 2 children, plus a €70.90 child tax credit (Kinderabsetzbetrag) paid out with it. Extra €121.40 school-start payment each September from age 6.
policies.value: ≈ €445/month for a newborn + a toddler (2026)
policies.eligibility: All residents with children living in their household; paid automatically after birth registration.
policies.caveat: Amounts frozen for 2026 and 2027 (no inflation adjustment); a real-terms cut of roughly 3% per year.

policies.name: Familienbonus Plus
policies.what: Tax credit of €2,000.16 per child per year (€166.68/month) under 18, deducted directly from income tax; can be split 50/50 between parents or taken fully by one. Parents with too little tax owe get the Kindermehrbetrag (up to €700/child) instead.
policies.value: ≈ €4,000/year (≈ €333/month) for 2 kids, as long as the household pays at least that much income tax — true for a median full-time earner
policies.eligibility: Anyone receiving Familienbeihilfe for the child and paying Austrian income tax; claim via employer or annual tax return.
policies.caveat: Worth the full amount only if the claiming parent's income tax is at least €2,000 per child; during a year of parental leave the working parent should claim 100%.

policies.name: Kindergarten: free mandatory year (national) + free all-day kindergarten in Vienna
policies.what: Nationwide, the last year before school (from age 5) is compulsory and free for 20 hours/week. Most Länder add free half-day places from about age 2.5–3. Vienna, Burgenland and Carinthia go further: all-day municipal and subsidised private kindergarten free from about age 1 until school; in Vienna parents pay only meals (roughly €80/month).
policies.value: In Vienna ≈ €0 fees for 2 full-day places (meals ≈ €80/month each); elsewhere roughly €100–€400/month per full-day place, more for under-3s
policies.eligibility: Vienna: child and one parent with main residence in Vienna. Mandatory year: all 5-year-olds.
policies.caveat: No legal entitlement to a place anywhere in Austria; only about one in three under-3s has a place (2024), fewer in rural areas; many rural kindergartens close at lunchtime or in summer.

policies.name: Papamonat + Familienzeitbonus
policies.what: Fathers may take 28–31 days off work immediately after the birth (Papamonat, job protected) and receive the Familienzeitbonus of €54.87/day (2026) from the health-insurance fund; employer pays nothing. The bonus is later offset against the father's own Kinderbetreuungsgeld if he takes any.
policies.value: ≈ €1,540–€1,700 for one month at home after each birth
policies.eligibility: Employed fathers insured for 182 days before birth, living in the same household, fully off work for the month.
policies.caveat: About 55–65% of a median net wage, and it is deducted from any Kinderbetreuungsgeld the father later claims; rate frozen for 2026–2027.

official.label: oesterreich.gv.at — Financial support for families (English)

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU social protection, family benefits)

BE.note: Belgium (figures below are for Flanders, where child benefit and childcare are regional; Wallonia and Brussels run similar but separately priced schemes) gives this household a universal child benefit of about €380/month for two children, income-priced crèches and free kleuterschool from age 2.5, which cuts the expensive childcare phase to roughly two years per child. Leave is short and flat-rate after maternity: parental leave pays only about €1,000/month. The real constraint is supply: subsidised crèche places in Flemish cities have multi-month waiting lists, and rent support is not available at two median wages.

headline.cash: ≈ €381/month for 2 kids (Groeipakket basisbedrag €190.66 each from Sept 2026) + €1,311 birth grant
headline.leave: 15 weeks maternity (82% then 75%, capped); 20 days birth leave; 4 months parental leave per parent at ≈ €1,000/month flat
headline.childcare: kleuterschool free from age 2.5; crèche fee income-based, roughly €25-30/day at two median wages (max €35.89)
headline.tax: extra tax-free allowance €5,230 for 2 kids (2026 income) + 45% tax reduction on childcare costs up to €16.90/day/child

policies.name: Kinderopvang met inkomenstarief + free kleuteronderwijs from 2.5
policies.what: Subsidised crèches charge a legally set day price based on joint taxable income: €6.47 to €35.89 per full day (2026), with a discount per extra dependent child; at two median wages expect roughly €25-30/day (~€500-600/month full time), 45% of which comes back as a tax reduction. From age 2.5 children enter kleuterschool, which is free (small materials bill only).
policies.value: ≈ €500-600/month for the baby in crèche (before tax reduction); ≈ €0 for the toddler from age 2.5
policies.eligibility: All families; request an attest inkomenstarief via mijn.opgroeien.be before the child starts; kleuterschool open to every child from 2.5.
policies.caveat: Places are the problem: Flemish subsidised crèches have waiting lists of 6-12 months in cities and the sector lost capacity in 2023-24; non-subsidised crèches charge a free market price (~€35-45/day), partly offset by a €3.78/day kinderopvangtoeslag. The fee scale is indexed +3.27% on 1 October 2026.

policies.name: Groeipakket (Flemish child benefit): startbedrag + basisbedrag
policies.what: Universal, non-means-tested monthly benefit of €190.66 per child born from 2019 (from 1 Sept 2026; €184.62 before), plus a one-off birth grant (startbedrag) of €1,310.75 per child and a small yearly school bonus, paid by a licensed payer (e.g. FONS, Parentia). A means-tested sociale toeslag stops at €49,024 gross taxable family income for 1-2 children, below two median wages.
policies.value: ≈ €381/month for 2 kids + €1,311 per birth (2026)
policies.eligibility: Every child domiciled in Flanders; no income test for the basic amount.
policies.caveat: Regional: Wallonia and Brussels pay comparable but different amounts under their own schemes. Indexed only once a year (September).

policies.name: Moederschapsrust, geboorteverlof and ouderschapsverlof
policies.what: Maternity: 15 weeks at 82% of gross pay for 30 days (uncapped), then 75% (capped), via the health insurer. Birth leave for the father/co-parent: 20 days, 3 at full employer pay, the rest at 82% (capped). Parental leave: 4 months per parent, full- or part-time, until age 12, at a flat RVA/ONEM allowance of €1,080 gross (≈ €970 net) monthly.
policies.value: ≈ 3.5 months at ~80% pay for the mother, 4 weeks for the father, then up to 8 months of flat ≈ €1,000/month between the two
policies.eligibility: Employees with recent insured work; parental leave needs 12 months with the current employer in the last 15.
policies.caveat: The parental-leave allowance replaces less than a third of a median wage, so most couples take it part-time (1/5 or half-time) rather than as a block.

policies.name: Verhoogde belastingvrije som for children + belastingvermindering kinderopvang
policies.what: Each taxpayer's tax-free allowance (€11,180 for 2026 income) is raised by €2,030 for one dependent child and €5,230 for two, relieved at the lowest bracket rates. Separately, 45% of childcare costs for children under 14 is refunded as a tax reduction, on up to €16.90 per day per child (2025 income; indexed yearly), covering crèche, childminder and holiday care.
policies.value: ≈ €1,300-1,900/year from the child allowance + up to ≈ €1,650/year per child in full-time crèche
policies.eligibility: All resident taxpayers; childcare reduction needs the yearly fiscal attest from the crèche or care provider.
policies.caveat: Only care provided by licensed/registered providers qualifies; the reduction is received the year after the cost, via the tax return.

official.label: Vlaanderen.be — Gezin, welzijn en gezondheid (kinderopvang, Groeipakket)

guide.label: MISSOC — comparative tables on family benefits (EU)

BG.note: Bulgaria (euro since 1 Jan 2026) gives a young working family two big things: one of Europe's longest earnings-related maternity leaves (410 days at 90%) followed by a flat benefit until age 2, and fully free public kindergartens and nurseries since April 2022. Cash child allowances are small and means-tested at a level (€466 net per family member) that a two-median-wage household only just misses or just meets. The 2026 budget froze the second-year benefit at €398.81 (a proposed rise to €460 was dropped) and kindergarten places in Sofia remain short.

headline.cash: one-off €191.74 (1st) + €460.17 (2nd child) birth grant; monthly €56.25 for 2 kids only if net income ≤ €466/family member
headline.leave: 410 days at 90% of pay (cap €2,300 insured income), then €398.81/month flat to age 2; 15 days paternity at 90%
headline.childcare: public nurseries (from 10 months) and kindergartens free of all fees incl. meals since April 2022; shortage of places in Sofia
headline.tax: taxable income reduced by €6,135.50 for 2 children → €613.55/year less income tax

policies.name: Обезщетение за бременност и раждане + отглеждане на дете до 2 г. (maternity and child-raising benefit)
policies.what: Insured mothers get 410 calendar days (45 before birth) at 90% of their average insurable income of the previous 24 months (income capped at €2,111.64/month, €2,300 from 1 Aug 2026). After that, leave until the child's 2nd birthday at a flat €398.81/month (2026). Fathers get 15 days at 90% after the birth and may take over the leave from the child's 6th month.
policies.value: ≈ €900-1,000/month for 13.5 months for a mother earning a median gross wage of roughly €1,100, then €398.81/month for ~10 more months; father +15 days at 90%
policies.eligibility: 12 months of insurance for general sickness and maternity; paid by the National Social Security Institute (НОИ).
policies.url_label: НОИ (National Social Security Institute) — maternity benefit
policies.caveat: The second-year flat benefit was frozen at €398.81 in the 2026 budget after a proposed increase to €460.17 was dropped; a parent who returns to work before age 2 keeps only 50% of it (€199.41/month).

policies.name: Безплатни детски ясли и градини (fee-free public nurseries and kindergartens)
policies.what: Since 1 April 2022 the state budget pays all parental fees, including meals, in municipal and state nurseries (from about 10 months) and kindergartens (from 3; preschool compulsory from 4). Families whose child gets no municipal place can claim compensation of up to €296.57/month (order of April 2025) towards a private nursery, kindergarten or licensed childminder, from 3 months of age until 1st grade.
policies.value: ≈ €0/month for two children in public care (private places cost €400-800/month); up to €296.57/month compensation if no public place is offered
policies.eligibility: All children with Bulgarian residence; admission by municipal ranking (Sofia: ИСОДЗ system).
policies.url_label: Sofia Municipality — kindergarten/nursery admission and compensation system (ИСОДЗ)
policies.caveat: Sofia and a few large cities still have thousands of unplaced 1-3-year-olds each year; the compensation covers only part of a private fee and requires a rejected municipal application.

policies.name: Данъчно облекчение за деца (child income-tax relief)
policies.what: One parent per child deducts a fixed sum from the annual taxable income: €3,067.75 for one child, €6,135.50 for two, €9,203.25 for three or more (2026 State Budget Act, same as the 2023-2025 levels). With Bulgaria's 10% flat income tax this returns €306.78, €613.55 or €920.33 a year, claimed via the employer in December or in the annual return.
policies.value: ≈ €613.55/year (≈ €51/month) back for 2 children
policies.eligibility: Resident parent with taxable income and no unpaid public debts; child under 18 and resident in the EU/EEA.
policies.url_label: НАП (National Revenue Agency) — Данъчни облекчения за деца
policies.caveat: The relief cannot exceed the parent's actual tax paid; a parent on maternity leave all year has no taxable income to set it against, so the other parent should claim both children.

policies.name: Еднократна помощ при раждане + месечни помощи за деца (birth grant and means-tested child allowance)
policies.what: Universal one-off birth grant of €191.74 for a 1st child, €460.17 for a 2nd, €230.09 for a 3rd (2026). Monthly family allowance until secondary school of €25.57 for one child or €56.25 for two, plus €102.26/month for a child under 1, are paid only if average net income per family member is at most €415 (full amount) or €466 (80%).
policies.value: €651.91 one-off for two births; €56.25/month (2 children) + €102.26/month (child under 1) only if family net income per member ≤ €466 — a two-median-wage couple with 2 children is right at that line
policies.eligibility: Birth grant: all resident mothers, no income test. Monthly allowances: income test, child attending school/vaccinated, applied at the Social Assistance Agency (АСП).
policies.url_label: АСП (Social Assistance Agency) — Семейни помощи за деца
policies.caveat: Monthly allowances are tiny by EU standards and the income ceiling (€466) rises only with the minimum wage; most two-earner families above the median receive nothing beyond the birth grant.

official.label: Social Assistance Agency — family benefits for children

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Bulgaria

CH.note: Switzerland is the weakest of the German-speaking countries for a young wage-earning family: high wages, but only 14 weeks of maternity leave, 2 weeks for the father, no paid parental leave at all, and childcare that costs CHF 110–150 per child per day before subsidies. Family allowances (at least CHF 215 per child per month) are the one reliable universal cash benefit. Subsidies for childcare and health-insurance premiums are cantonal and income-tested, so two median earners often get little; a new federal childcare allowance of up to CHF 500 per child per month was passed in 2025 and is expected from 2027.

headline.cash: ≥ CHF 430/month (≈ €460) for 2 kids (Kinderzulage min CHF 215 each; up to CHF 300+ in VS/GE/VD/ZG)
headline.leave: 14 weeks maternity + 2 weeks paternity at 80% (max CHF 220/day); no parental leave
headline.childcare: no entitlement; full cost ≈ CHF 110–150/day; cantonal subsidies income-tested; federal Betreuungszulage up to CHF 500/child/month expected 2027
headline.tax: federal deductions: childcare costs up to CHF 25,800/child, Kinderabzug CHF 6,800 (2025)

policies.name: Familienzulagen (Kinderzulage / Ausbildungszulage)
policies.what: Monthly child allowance paid through the employer's family-compensation fund: federal minimum CHF 215 per child under 16 and CHF 268 in education (since 2025, unchanged 2026). Cantons may pay more; Valais, Geneva, Vaud and Zug pay over CHF 300. One allowance per child, no income test.
policies.value: CHF 430–600+/month (≈ €460–640) for 2 kids depending on canton, 2026
policies.eligibility: All employees (and self-employed) with children; claimed via the employer; one parent per child.
policies.caveat: Amounts vary by canton of employment, not residence; the federal minimum has only been raised once (2025) since 2009.

policies.name: Mutterschaftsentschädigung + Vaterschaftsurlaub (EO)
policies.what: Mothers: 14 weeks (98 days) after birth at 80% of previous earnings, max CHF 220/day (≈ CHF 6,600/month), from the loss-of-earnings scheme (EO). Fathers/other parent: 2 weeks (10 working days) within 6 months of birth at the same 80% rate. There is no statutory parental leave after that; unpaid leave depends on the employer.
policies.value: ≈ CHF 5,400/month for 3.2 months for a median-wage mother (≈ CHF 17,000, ≈ €18,000) + ≈ CHF 2,500 for the father's 2 weeks
policies.eligibility: Insured for 9 months before birth and worked at least 5 months of that; job protected for 16 weeks after birth.
policies.caveat: Shortest paid leave in Western Europe; a mother who stops working after 14 weeks receives nothing further; many employers top up, but that is not a right.

policies.name: Cantonal/communal Kita subsidies + new federal Betreuungszulage (UKibeG)
policies.what: No legal entitlement to a place; a Kita day costs roughly CHF 110–150. Cities subsidise by income: in Zurich the parent share runs from about CHF 12 to CHF 120 per day. The federal UKibeG (passed Dec 2025, final July 2026, expected 2027) adds a care allowance of CHF 100/month per weekly care day, max CHF 500/child/month, until age 8.
policies.value: Today ≈ CHF 2,500–3,500/month net for 2 kids at 3 days/week for two median earners (small or no subsidy); from ~2027 minus up to CHF 600/month Betreuungszulage
policies.eligibility: Subsidies: residents of the commune, both parents working, income below cantonal ceilings. Betreuungszulage: child in a licensed crèche, daycare family or after-school care.
policies.caveat: Subsidy ceilings differ by commune and often phase out around a two-earner median income; waiting lists in cities; the federal allowance's start date is not yet fixed.

policies.name: Federal and cantonal child tax deductions
policies.what: Direct federal tax (tax year 2025): documented third-party childcare costs deductible up to CHF 25,800 per child under 14; general child deduction CHF 6,800 per child; CHF 263 per child off the tax bill (Elterntarif); extra insurance deduction per child. Cantons grant their own, usually smaller, childcare and child deductions.
policies.value: Roughly CHF 1,000–3,000/year less tax for 2 kids in full-time paid childcare, depending on canton and income
policies.eligibility: All taxpayers with dependent children; childcare deduction requires both parents working (or in training) and receipts.
policies.caveat: Federal tax is a small share of Swiss income tax; the big cantonal deductions vary from about CHF 10,000 to 25,000 for childcare.

policies.name: Prämienverbilligung for children's health-insurance premiums
policies.what: Health insurance is compulsory and paid per person, including children (average child premium about CHF 120/month in 2026). Cantons must reduce children's premiums by at least 80% for families with lower and middle incomes, and reduce adults' premiums on a sliding scale; thresholds and procedures are cantonal.
policies.value: Up to ≈ CHF 200/month saved on 2 children's premiums if the household is under the cantonal ceiling
policies.eligibility: Set by each canton on taxable income and household size; some cantons pay automatically, others require an application.
policies.caveat: A two-median-earner family qualifies in some cantons and not in others; premiums rose 4.4% on average for 2026.

official.label: ch.ch — Family and partnership (federal portal)

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EFTA social protection)

CY.note: Cyprus has built its family package quickly since 2022: 22 weeks of maternity allowance at 72–80% of earnings, 8 paid weeks of parental leave per parent, an EU-funded nursery subsidy for under-4s and, from 2026, a higher tax-free threshold with per-child deductions. Ongoing cash is modest and means-tested: a dual-median-income couple (≈ €51,000 gross, CYSTAT median €1,968/month) sits in the lowest child-benefit band and loses it entirely above €59,000. There is no legal childcare entitlement before compulsory pre-primary (entry age being lowered from 4y8m towards 4 by 2032/33); nursery capacity and fees vary, and there is no rent support at this income.

headline.cash: ≈ €75/month child benefit for 2 kids at ~€50k income (2026), €1,095 + €1,643 birth grants
headline.leave: 22 weeks maternity at 72–80% of earnings; 2 weeks paternity; 8 paid weeks parental leave per parent
headline.childcare: nursery subsidy €100–350/child/month (up to 80% of fees) for child-benefit families; free pre-primary from ~4.5
headline.tax: 2026 reform: tax-free €22,000 (was €19,500), €1,000 + €1,250 child deductions per parent, up to €2,000 rent deduction

policies.name: Nursery/kindergarten tuition subsidy for children up to 4 (Deputy Ministry of Social Welfare)
policies.what: Since 2024/25 an EU Recovery-funded scheme pays up to 80% of monthly nursery fees for under-4s enrolled in a participating public or private nursery: €100–€350 per child per month depending on family income and number of children, paid to families that receive child benefit. A second scheme pays 100% of fees (cap €130 public / €200 private per month) for 4-year-olds until they enter free compulsory pre-primary. 2026/27 applications opened 7 September 2026.
policies.value: roughly €100–€200 per child per month at ~€50,000 income (≈ €2,400–4,800/yr for 2 kids); up to €350/child for lower incomes
policies.eligibility: Families entitled to child benefit for the year (income ≤ €59,000 with 2 children); child enrolled in a nursery that joined the scheme.
policies.url_label: gov.cy — Tuition subsidy for children up to 4 (parents)
policies.caveat: Annual, budget-limited scheme (~25,000 children, €22m); tied to the child-benefit income cut-off, so a pay rise above €59,000 removes both. Free compulsory pre-primary currently starts at 4 years 6 months (2025/26), reaching age 4 only by 2032/33.

policies.name: Maternity allowance (22 weeks) + paternity allowance + paid parental leave
policies.what: Social Insurance pays maternity allowance for 22 weeks for a first or second child (26 weeks from the third) at 72% of insurable earnings, rising to 80% with one dependant and 90% with two. Fathers get 2 consecutive weeks of paternity allowance on the same basis. Each parent also has 18 weeks of parental leave per child, of which 8 weeks are paid at 72% (max 5 weeks per year since 2025), usable until the child is 15.
policies.value: ≈ €8,000–9,000 maternity pay on a €2,000/month wage, ≈ €700 paternity, plus ≈ €2,900 per parent for the 8 paid parental-leave weeks
policies.eligibility: Insured employees and self-employed with at least 26 weeks of contributions; parental-leave allowance needs 12 months' work in the last 2 years.
policies.url_label: Social Insurance Services — maternity, paternity and parental-leave allowances
policies.caveat: Employers are not obliged to top up to full pay; the remaining 10 weeks of parental leave are unpaid; fathers report multi-month processing waits.

policies.name: Child benefit (Επίδομα τέκνου) + childbirth grant
policies.what: Annual means-tested child benefit from the Welfare Benefits Administration Service. For 2 children (2025 table) it is €718 per child if family income is ≤ €19,500, €655 up to €39,000, €479 up to €49,000 and €435 up to €59,000, nothing above; 2026 bands are indexed (≈ €705/€643 in the lower bands, cut-offs €21,500/€41,000). Childbirth grant from Social Insurance: €1,095 for the first child, €1,643 for the second (2026).
policies.value: ≈ €870–960/yr (≈ €75/month) for 2 children at ~€50,000 income + €2,738 in birth grants over two births
policies.eligibility: Residents; family income ≤ €59,000 with 2 children (≤ €49,000 with one); assets ≤ €1.2m; birth grant needs 26 weeks of insurance by mother or father.
policies.url_label: gov.cy — Child benefit and single-parent family benefit
policies.caveat: Sharp cliff-edge at €59,000 for a 2-child family. A reform approved by Cabinet in September 2026 for January 2027 raises payments by 10% (income ≤ €22,000) or 5% (≤ €44,000) and widens thresholds mainly for families with 3+ children; it still needs Parliament.

policies.name: 2026 tax reform: higher tax-free threshold + child and rent deductions
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 the personal tax-free threshold rose from €19,500 to €22,000 (then 20% to €32,000, 25% to €42,000, 30% to €72,000, 35% above). New deductions per parent: €1,000 for the first child and €1,250 for the second (family income ≤ €100,000), plus up to €2,000 a year for rent or mortgage interest on the main home.
policies.value: roughly €900–1,500/yr less income tax for a dual-earner couple with 2 children versus 2025
policies.eligibility: All resident taxpayers; child deductions per parent within the income bands; rent deduction for the main residence.
policies.caveat: Deductions are worth only their marginal rate (20% for most median earners), and a parent earning under €22,000 gets nothing from them.

official.label: Social Insurance Services — family allowances (maternity, paternity, birth grant)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Cyprus

CZ.note: Czechia gives a big, flexible lump of money per child (350,000 CZK parental allowance, drawn over up to 3 years while the parent may keep working) and a refundable child tax credit, but there is no universal child benefit any more: since 2025/26 the old child allowance and housing allowance were folded into one means-tested 'superdávka' that a two-earner median household is usually just above. Public kindergarten from age 3 is cheap and a place is guaranteed, but care for under-3s is scarce and expensive. Renters get no help unless income falls below the superdávka line.

headline.cash: 350,000 CZK (≈ €14,300) parental allowance per child, drawn flexibly until age 3; no universal monthly child benefit
headline.leave: 28 weeks maternity at 70% (≈ 27,000 CZK/month at median wage); 2 weeks paternity at 70%; father may take maternity benefit from week 7
headline.childcare: kindergarten: guaranteed place from age 3, fee max 8% of minimum wage (≤ 1,792 CZK/month, 2026), free last year; under-3 care scarce
headline.tax: refundable child tax credit 15,204 + 22,320 CZK/year for two children (≈ 3,100 CZK/month, ≈ €128)

policies.name: Rodičovský příspěvek (parental allowance)
policies.what: A fixed pot of 350,000 CZK per child (700,000 CZK for multiples) for children born from 1 January 2024, paid monthly at a pace the parent chooses — up to 70% of 30× the daily assessment base (roughly the maternity-benefit level) for insured parents, 13,000 CZK/month max for the uninsured — until the child turns 3. The parent may work; an under-2 may attend nursery up to 92 hours/month without losing it.
policies.value: 700,000 CZK (≈ €28,500) for two children; e.g. ≈ 9,700 CZK/month per child if spread over 3 years, or ≈ 27,000 CZK/month for ~13 months
policies.eligibility: Any parent permanently resident in Czechia caring for the youngest child; no income test, no prior employment needed (only the monthly cap differs).
policies.caveat: Only one allowance per family at a time (for the youngest child), so a second baby ends the first child's unspent balance in effect — draw fast. A rise to 400,000 CZK for children born from 2027 has been reported; verify before relying on it.

policies.name: Peněžitá pomoc v mateřství (maternity benefit) + otcovská (paternity benefit)
policies.what: Sickness-insurance benefit of 70% of the (reduced) daily assessment base for 28 weeks (37 for multiples), starting 6–8 weeks before the due date. From week 7 the father may take the benefit instead of the mother. Separately the father gets 14 days of otcovská at 70% within the first 6 weeks. Both are tax-free.
policies.value: ≈ 27,000 CZK/month (≈ €1,100) for 6.5 months at a median wage (~40,000 CZK gross); father ≈ 12,500 CZK for his 2 weeks
policies.eligibility: 270 days of sickness insurance in the last 2 years (employees are insured automatically); self-employed only if they pay voluntary sickness insurance.
policies.caveat: The daily base is reduced above ~1,550 CZK/day (2026 bands), so replacement falls below 70% for above-average earners.

policies.name: Daňové zvýhodnění na dítě (child tax credit, refundable)
policies.what: Annual income-tax credit of 15,204 CZK for the first child, 22,320 CZK for the second, 27,840 CZK for each further child (2026; double for a ZTP/P child), applied monthly by the employer. If the credit exceeds the tax due, the difference is paid out as a 'daňový bonus'. Claimed by one parent for all children.
policies.value: 37,524 CZK/year (≈ €1,530) for two children — about 3,100 CZK per month
policies.eligibility: A parent with annual earned income of at least 6× the minimum wage (124,800 CZK in 2026); child under 18 (26 if studying) living in the household.
policies.caveat: The separate nursery-fee credit (školkovné, up to ~17,000 CZK/year) was abolished from 2024.

policies.name: Mateřská škola (public kindergarten) — guaranteed place from age 3, low fee
policies.what: Children have a legal right to a place in their catchment public kindergarten from age 3 (from 2 only if capacity allows). The monthly fee is set by the municipality but capped at 8% of the minimum wage — max 1,792 CZK in 2026, typically 500–1,000 CZK — plus meals (~1,000 CZK). The final year before school (age 5–6) is compulsory and free.
policies.value: Full-day public kindergarten for roughly 1,500–2,800 CZK/month (≈ €60–115) per child including meals, free in the last year
policies.eligibility: All children from age 3 with residence in the municipality; priority by age.
policies.caveat: Under-3 care (jesle, dětské skupiny) is scarce and costs roughly 3,000–8,000 CZK/month; big-city kindergartens still turn away 3-year-olds when full despite the entitlement.

policies.name: Superdávka (dávka státní sociální pomoci) — child bonus + rent component
policies.what: From October 2025 the child allowance, housing allowance, subsistence allowance and housing supplement were merged into one means-tested benefit; old benefits stopped in mid-2026. It has four parts: living costs, housing (covers rent above a set share of income), a child bonus (basic ~1,000 CZK per child) and a work bonus. Assessed on household income, assets and work activity.
policies.value: ≈ 2,000 CZK/month child bonus for two kids plus part of the rent — but only while household net income is below roughly 54,000 CZK/month (4× the family's living minimum)
policies.eligibility: Households with dependent children whose net income is under 4× the living minimum and where every adult is work-active (or on parental leave); assets are checked.
policies.caveat: Two full-time median earners are typically just above the line; it becomes reachable when one parent is on parental allowance. New system with long processing times in 2026.

official.label: Úřad práce ČR / MPSV — state social support (family benefits)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Czechia

DE.note: Germany combines a solid universal child benefit (€259/child/month in 2026), a well-designed parental allowance (Elterngeld, up to €1,800/month for 12+2 months) and a legal right to a childcare place from age one. The catch is that the right exists on paper: several hundred thousand Kita places are missing, above all in the West, and fees range from zero (Berlin, Rhineland-Palatinate) to several hundred euros a month. Housing benefit (Wohngeld) is not reachable for two median earners, and married-couple tax splitting helps only if the partners' incomes differ a lot.

headline.cash: €518/month for 2 kids (Kindergeld €259 each, 2026)
headline.leave: Elterngeld 65% of net (max €1,800/month) for 12 + 2 partner months; 14 weeks Mutterschutz at full pay
headline.childcare: legal right to a Kita place from age 1; fees €0 (Berlin) to a few hundred €/month; ~400,000 places missing
headline.tax: 80% of childcare fees deductible up to €4,800/child; Kinderfreibetrag €9,756/child (rarely beats Kindergeld at median)

policies.name: Elterngeld (Basiselterngeld / ElterngeldPlus)
policies.what: Parental allowance replacing 65% of previous net income (67% for low earners), min €300, max €1,800/month, for 12 months, plus 2 partner months if the other parent takes at least 2 months. ElterngeldPlus stretches each month into two at half the rate, usable alongside part-time work. Sibling bonus +10% (min €75) while an older child is under 3.
policies.value: ≈ €1,700/month for ~12–14 months per child at median net pay (≈ €22,000–24,000 per child), plus 10% sibling bonus for the second child
policies.eligibility: Parents living with the child and working at most 32 h/week; taxable household income below €175,000/year (births from April 2025).
policies.caveat: €1,800 cap has not been raised since 2007; Elternzeit (job protection) runs up to 3 years but is unpaid beyond Elterngeld.

policies.name: Kindergeld
policies.what: Universal monthly child benefit of €259 per child (raised from €255 in January 2026), paid by the Familienkasse until age 18 (25 in education), no income test. Low-income families can add Kinderzuschlag (up to roughly €300/child), but two median earners are above its limit.
policies.value: €518/month (€6,216/year) for 2 kids, 2026
policies.eligibility: All parents resident in Germany; one application per child at the Familienkasse.
policies.caveat: Kindergeld is an advance on the child tax allowance; the tax office keeps whichever is better (Günstigerprüfung), so the two do not add up.

policies.name: Legal right to a Kita place from age 1 (§ 24 SGB VIII) + Land fee reductions
policies.what: Every child from its first birthday has an enforceable right to a place in a Kita or with a childminder; the Jugendamt must provide one. Fees are set by Länder and municipalities: Berlin fully free, Hamburg 5 h/day free, Rhineland-Palatinate free from 2, NRW free in the last 2 years, elsewhere income-graded fees.
policies.value: Roughly €0 (Berlin) to €300–€500/month per full-time place for a median family in Bavaria or Baden-Württemberg, more for under-3s; 2 kids can mean €0–€900/month
policies.eligibility: All children from age 1 (from birth if parents work); apply to the municipality, often a year ahead.
policies.caveat: Bertelsmann Stiftung estimates roughly 400,000 places missing (2024/25), mostly in western Länder; opening hours often end mid-afternoon; parents can sue but a court cannot conjure a place.

policies.name: Mutterschutz + Kinderkrankengeld
policies.what: Maternity protection: 6 weeks before and 8 weeks after birth off work at full net pay (health fund pays €13/day, employer tops up), with dismissal ban. Child-sick leave: each parent may stay home 15 paid days per child per year (max 35 for several children) at 90% of net pay, for children under 12.
policies.value: ≈ 14 weeks of full pay per birth; up to 30 paid days/year per parent for 2 sick kids
policies.eligibility: Employees in statutory health insurance (about 90% of workers); children co-insured free of charge.
policies.caveat: The 15-day Kinderkrankengeld rule is a temporary extension valid to end-2026; from 2027 it may fall back to 10 days unless prolonged.

policies.name: Childcare-cost deduction, Kinderfreibetrag and Ehegattensplitting
policies.what: 80% of paid childcare fees (Kita, childminder) are deductible as special expenses up to €4,800 per child per year (from 2025). The Kinderfreibetrag (€9,756 per child in 2026) is set against Kindergeld and only wins for high earners. Married couples file jointly (splitting), which lowers tax when one partner earns much less, e.g. part-time after a birth.
policies.value: Up to ≈ €1,400 tax saved per child per year on Kita fees at a 30% marginal rate; splitting worth roughly €1,000–3,000/year when one partner goes part-time
policies.eligibility: Anyone filing an income-tax return; splitting requires marriage or registered partnership.
policies.caveat: Unmarried couples get no splitting; the childcare deduction is worthless in Länder where Kita is already free.

official.label: Familienportal des Bundes (all federal family benefits)

guide.label: EU Your Europe — Family benefits

DK.note: Denmark delivers most of its family support in kind: a guaranteed, heavily subsidised crèche place from 26 weeks, free healthcare and child dental care, and 24 weeks of paid leave per parent (often topped up to full pay by collective agreements). Cash is modest and there is no family tax splitting; the income-tested childcare and housing benefits are out of reach for two median earners, and Copenhagen rents are high. From 1 January 2027 the parent share of childcare cost falls from 25% to 21.3%.

headline.cash: ≈ 3,580 kr/month (≈ €480) tax-free for two children under 3 (børne- og ungeydelse, 2026)
headline.leave: 24 weeks paid leave per parent after birth (48 shared) + 4 weeks before; state benefit max 5,085 kr/week, employers often top up to full pay
headline.childcare: guaranteed place from 26 weeks; parents pay max 25% of cost (21.3% from 2027) — Copenhagen crèche 3,555 kr/month, 50% sibling discount
headline.tax: no family tax splitting or child tax credit; only the transferable personal allowance between spouses

policies.name: Dagtilbud: pasningsgaranti + fee cap + søskendetilskud
policies.what: Municipalities must offer a childcare place from age 26 weeks (pasningsgaranti). Parents pay at most 25% of the gross operating cost (21.3% from 1 Jan 2027); the state/municipality covers the rest. Copenhagen 2026: crèche (0–2 y) 3,555 kr/month, kindergarten (3–5 y) 1,988 kr, lunch extra. 50% sibling discount on the cheaper place.
policies.value: ≈ 5,300 kr/month (≈ €715) for two crèche places in Copenhagen; the subsidy is worth ≈ 10,600 kr/month per place
policies.eligibility: All resident children; income-tested free places (fripladstilskud) only below 677,500 kr household income (2026), i.e. not at two median wages.
policies.caveat: Fees vary by municipality (crèche typically 3,300–4,500 kr/month in 2026); places may be offered far from home; staffing ratios (minimumsnormeringer) still uneven.

policies.name: Barselsorlov + barselsdagpenge
policies.what: Since Aug 2022 each parent gets 24 weeks of paid leave after birth (mother also 4 weeks before). For employees 11 weeks per parent are earmarked (2 right after birth + 9 non-transferable); 13 weeks each can be transferred. State benefit (barselsdagpenge) is up to 5,085 kr/week in 2026 (≈ 22,000 kr/month); most collective agreements top up to full salary for a large part of the leave.
policies.value: 48 weeks shared paid leave; ≈ 22,000 kr/month (≈ €2,950) from the state ≈ 47% of a 47,000 kr median wage, often 100% with employer top-up
policies.eligibility: Employees with 160 hours in the 4 months before leave (also self-employed/unemployed with other rules).
policies.caveat: Without a collective agreement the state rate is a big pay cut at median wage; earmarked weeks not used by a parent are lost.

policies.name: Børne- og ungeydelse (child and youth benefit)
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, paid quarterly by Udbetaling Danmark and split between the parents. 2026 rates: 5,370 kr/quarter per child aged 0–2, 4,251 kr for 3–6 (lower for 7–17). Reduced by 2% of each parent's own income above 961,100 kr (2026), so untouched at median wages.
policies.value: ≈ 3,580 kr/month (≈ €480) for a newborn + toddler; ≈ 3,200 kr once one child turns 3
policies.eligibility: Residents with children under 18; full rate after 6 years' residence/work in DK/EEA (phased in otherwise).

policies.name: Free child healthcare, health visitor and dental care
policies.what: GP, hospital and 7 free preventive child examinations (age 0–5) plus vaccinations are free. A municipal health visitor (sundhedsplejerske) makes home visits in the baby's first year. Municipal dental care is free for children and young people up to age 22 (extension to 18–21-year-olds phased in 2022–2025). Public school (folkeskole) is free.
policies.value: ≈ 0 kr out of pocket for child health and dental care
policies.eligibility: All residents with a Danish health card (sundhedskort).
policies.caveat: Adult dental care is not free; school lunch is not provided free nationally.

official.label: Life in Denmark (official English portal) — family and children

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EEA social protection)

EE.note: Estonia's big instrument is time, not cash: 605 days of parental benefit at 100% of each parent's previous pay, usable flexibly until the child is 3, with a guaranteed municipal kindergarten place from 18 months. Universal child allowance is modest (€80/child) and the child-specific income-tax exemption was abolished from the 2024 tax year; there is no housing benefit reachable at median wage. Kindergarten fees are capped by law and Tallinn abolishes them for residents from September 2026; falling birth rates mean places are now generally available.

headline.cash: €160/month for 2 kids (child allowance €80 each) + €320 birth grant per child (2026)
headline.leave: 605 days at 100% of pay: 100 mother-only + 30 father-only + 475 shared, cap €3,806/month (2026)
headline.childcare: municipal place guaranteed from 18 months; fee capped at 20% of min. wage (€189/month), Tallinn free for residents from Sept 2026, food ≈ €4/day
headline.tax: none for children since tax year 2024; flat €700/month basic exemption per adult from 2026

policies.name: Parental benefit (vanemahüvitis): maternity + paternity + shared
policies.what: Mother gets 100 days (up to 70 before birth), father 30 non-transferable days, plus 475 shared days parents split freely, all paid at 100% of previous average earnings (2026 floor €886, ceiling €3,806/month gross). Usable day-by-day until the child turns 3; up to 60 days both parents together; working while receiving does not reduce it.
policies.value: ≈ 100% of each parent's wage for about 20 months combined; at a ~€1,900 gross median wage roughly €38,000 gross per child
policies.eligibility: Residents; amount based on social tax paid in the 12-month reference period, minimum-wage floor if no income.
policies.caveat: Ceiling cut from 3x to 2x the average wage from 2026 (irrelevant at median pay). Employer must grant the matching leave; the 30 paternity days cannot be worked.

policies.name: Child allowance (lapsetoetus) + childbirth allowance
policies.what: Universal, non-means-tested €80/month for the first and second child and €100/month from the third child, paid until age 19 (2026 rates). One-off childbirth allowance of €320 per child. Granted automatically after birth registration via the Social Insurance Board self-service portal.
policies.value: €160/month for 2 kids (€1,920/year) plus €640 one-off for two births
policies.eligibility: All permanent residents with children; no income test.
policies.caveat: Rates unchanged since 2023 and not indexed; the large-family allowance (€450/month) only starts at 3 children.

policies.name: Municipal kindergarten place from 18 months, fee capped by law
policies.what: Municipalities must offer every child aged 1.5–7 a kindergarten place (from Sept 2025: an offer two months before the parent returns to work). Parent fee is capped at 20% of the national minimum wage per child (€189.20/month from Sept 2026). Tallinn charged €50/month and abolishes the fee for registered residents from 1 Sept 2026; parents still pay food (≈ €2.80–4.01/day in Tallinn).
policies.value: Tallinn: ≈ €80/month per child for food only from Sept 2026; elsewhere fee + food typically well under €250/month
policies.eligibility: Children registered in the municipality; Tallinn exemption needs child and one parent registered in Tallinn.
policies.caveat: Fees outside Tallinn are set locally up to the cap. Preferred kindergartens still fill up; Tallinn scrapped waiting lists in 2026 and now assigns places automatically, sometimes at a different site than requested.

policies.name: Free child health care, dental care and school lunch
policies.what: All children under 19 are covered by the Health Insurance Fund regardless of parents' status; dental care is free until 19 at contracted dentists. General education is free including textbooks, and the state funds a hot school lunch (€1/day, topped up by municipalities so most schools charge parents nothing).
policies.value: ≈ €0 out of pocket for GP, hospital, dental and school lunches for both children
policies.eligibility: All children resident in Estonia.
policies.caveat: Only dentists with a Health Insurance Fund contract are free; prescription co-payments still apply.

official.label: Sotsiaalkindlustusamet — overview of family benefits

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Estonia

ES.note: Spain has no universal child benefit: the only regular cash for kids at a median wage is the refundable mother's tax credit for under-3s. The real strengths are parental leave (19 fully-paid weeks for EACH parent since 2025/26) and free public preschool from age 3. Public 0-3 places are free in a growing number of regions (Galicia, Asturias, Madrid, Valencia, Canarias) but scarce; rent support for under-35s exists on paper but is income-capped and chronically oversubscribed.

headline.cash: no universal child benefit; €100/month per child under 3 via the refundable maternity tax credit (+ up to €1,000/yr childcare top-up)
headline.leave: 19 weeks at 100% for EACH parent (17 + 2 flexible weeks, 2026); non-transferable
headline.childcare: free public preschool 3–6 nationwide; 0–3 free in several regions, otherwise income-scaled municipal fees; places scarce
headline.tax: mínimo por descendientes: €2,400/€2,700 per child + €2,800 extra per child under 3 kept tax-free

policies.name: Prestación por nacimiento y cuidado de menor (birth and childcare leave)
policies.what: Each parent gets 19 weeks paid at 100% of their contribution base (Royal Decree-law 9/2025): 6 weeks compulsory right after birth, 11 flexible weeks until the child turns 1, plus 2 extra weeks usable until age 8 (in force from 1 Jan 2026 for births since 2 Aug 2024). Not transferable; single parents get 32 weeks.
policies.value: ≈ 38 weeks of household income fully replaced per birth (two median earners); benefit is tax-exempt
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed registered with Social Security with a short minimum contribution record (none under 21; 90 days in last 7 years for ages 21–26).
policies.url_label: Seguridad Social — Prestación por nacimiento y cuidado de menor
policies.caveat: Payment capped at the maximum contribution base (≈ €4,900–5,100/month gross, 2025/26). A further 8-week 'permiso parental' until age 8 exists but is UNPAID.

policies.name: Free public preschool 3–6 (segundo ciclo de Educación Infantil) + regional free 0–3
policies.what: From the September after the child turns 3, a place in a public or state-funded (concertado) preschool is free of tuition nationwide (enrolment ~97%). For 0–3, public places are free in Galicia, Asturias, Madrid, Comunitat Valenciana and Canarias and partly in Andalucía; elsewhere municipal 'escuelas infantiles' charge income-scaled fees, typically €100–350/month.
policies.value: ≈ €3,000–6,000/yr saved per child once free; 0–3 saving depends on region and on getting a place
policies.eligibility: All resident children; 3–6 is a universal entitlement. 0–3 admission is by points (income, siblings, work status) and capacity.
policies.url_label: Eurydice (EU) — Early childhood education and care in Spain
policies.caveat: There is no legal entitlement to a 0–3 place; public 0–3 coverage is ~40% of children and waiting lists are the norm in big cities. Lunch, extended hours and materials are charged even in 'free' centres.

policies.name: Deducción por maternidad + incremento por gastos de guardería
policies.what: Refundable tax credit of €1,200/yr (paid as €100/month in advance on request, form 140) for each child under 3 to a mother who is employed, self-employed or on unemployment benefit. Plus up to €1,000/yr extra per child for fees paid to a licensed nursery (2025/26 rules).
policies.value: up to ≈ €4,400/yr for a newborn + toddler both under 3 if both attend a nursery; €2,400/yr without nursery
policies.eligibility: Mothers (or sole fathers) registered with Social Security; no income ceiling. Not combinable with the low-income child supplement (CAPI).
policies.caveat: The nursery top-up is limited to actual fees at an authorised centre and is claimed only in the annual return, not monthly.

policies.name: Mínimo por descendientes (child allowance in income tax)
policies.what: Part of income is shielded from tax per child: €2,400 (1st), €2,700 (2nd), €4,000 (3rd), €4,500 (4th+), plus €2,800 extra for every child under 3 (2025/26). Split between both parents. Joint filing gives an extra €3,400 reduction, useful only if one parent earns little.
policies.value: ≈ €2,000–2,600/yr less income tax for two median earners with two children under 3 (€10,700 shielded at a 19–24% marginal rate)
policies.eligibility: Children under 25 living with the taxpayer with income below €8,000.
policies.caveat: It reduces tax, so it is worth less to low earners; the €2,800 under-3 supplement disappears at the third birthday.

policies.name: Bono Alquiler Joven (young tenants' rent bonus)
policies.what: Monthly rent subsidy for tenants aged 18–35: €250/month for up to 2 years under the 2022–25 programme, rising to up to €300/month (or €200 for a room) in the State Housing Plan 2026–2030. Applicant income must not exceed 3× IPREM (≈ €25,200/yr gross, 2026); rent caps of roughly €600–900/month set by each region.
policies.value: ≈ €3,000–3,600/yr if you get it; most two-earner couples are close to or above the income cap
policies.eligibility: 18–35, legal residents, rental contract for main home, income ≤ 3× IPREM; applications run by the regions.
policies.url_label: Ministerio de Vivienda — Bono Alquiler Joven
policies.caveat: Funds are limited and calls in most regions closed within days or weeks in 2022–2025 with long backlogs; several regions had not opened the 2026 call by mid-2026.

official.label: Seguridad Social — family benefits portal (prestaciones.seg-social.es)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Spain

FI.note: Finland gives a two-earner couple a long, gender-equal paid leave (160 weekdays each plus 40 pregnancy days), a legal right to municipal daycare at a low income-tested fee, and a home-care allowance if one parent stays home until age 3. Cash benefits are the weak side: the child benefit index is frozen 2024–2027 and general housing allowance was cut in 2024 and is unreachable at two median wages; there is no family taxation. Wages are lower than in the other Nordics, but the neuvola clinics, free child healthcare and free school meals are reliable and universal.

headline.cash: ≈ 252 €/month lapsilisä for two under-3s (frozen until 2027); + 377.68 €/month home-care allowance if a parent stays home until age 3
headline.leave: 40 pregnancy days + 160 weekdays per parent (63 transferable) at ≈ 70% of wage; ≈ 14 months paid in total
headline.childcare: legal right to daycare from end of leave; income-tested fee, ≈ 180 €/month for two children at two median wages (max 335 + 134 € from Aug 2026)
headline.tax: none: individual taxation, no child tax credit

policies.name: Raskausraha + vanhempainraha (pregnancy and parental allowance)
policies.what: Since the 2022 reform: 40 weekdays of pregnancy allowance for the mother, then 160 weekdays of parental allowance for each parent (paid 6 days/week, ≈ 6.4 months each), of which 63 days can be transferred to the other parent. Rate ≈ 70% of annual earnings up to 43,567 €, 40% above; minimum 31.99 €/day (2026). Usable until the child turns 2.
policies.value: ≈ 2,600 €/month before tax at a 3,800 € median wage; 360 paid weekdays per child (≈ 14 months) shared by the couple
policies.eligibility: Covered by Finnish social security; income-based rate needs earnings in the reference year, otherwise minimum.
policies.caveat: Employer pays full salary only if the collective agreement says so (often 1–3 months); untransferred days of a parent are lost.

policies.name: Varhaiskasvatus (municipal early childhood education) with income-tested fee
policies.what: Every child has a legal right to a full-time municipal daycare place once parental allowance ends (≈ 9 months). Fee = 10.7% of gross family income above a threshold (6,399 €/month for a 4-person family from 1 Aug 2026), capped at 335 €/month for the youngest child; second child pays 40% (max 134 €); free below the threshold. Pre-primary (esiopetus) at 6 is free.
policies.value: ≈ 180 €/month for two full-time places at two median wages (≈ 7,600 € household income); at most 469 €/month
policies.eligibility: All resident children; fee depends on family size and gross income.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Education and Culture — ECEC client fees
policies.caveat: Big-city places can be far from home and staff shortages are common in Helsinki region; fee max rises from 311 € to 335 € on 1 Aug 2026.

policies.name: Lapsilisä (child benefit) + maternity grant
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, monthly until age 17: 94.88 € for the 1st child, 104.84 € for the 2nd, rising for further children, plus 26 € extra for each child under 3 (2026). Single parents get +73.30 €/child. Also a one-off maternity package or 170 € cash per birth. Index frozen 2024–2027.
policies.value: ≈ 252 €/month for a newborn + toddler; ≈ 200 €/month once both are 3+
policies.eligibility: All children resident in Finland; no income test.
policies.caveat: No inflation adjustment in 2024–2027 under the current government's savings package, a real-terms cut.

policies.name: Kotihoidon tuki (child home care allowance)
policies.what: If a child under 3 is not in municipal daycare after parental leave, the family gets 377.68 €/month for that child plus 113.07 € for each further under-3 sibling and 72.66 € for 3–6-year-old siblings (2026); an income-tested supplement of up to 202.12 € exists but phases out at ≈ 4,258 €/month family income. Taxable. A parent working ≤ 30 h/week can instead get flexible care allowance of 179–269 €/month.
policies.value: ≈ 491 €/month (taxable) if one parent stays home with the baby + toddler until the baby turns 3
policies.eligibility: Child under 3 not in municipal daycare; not payable for a child on whom parental allowance is paid.
policies.caveat: Some municipalities add a kuntalisä, many (incl. Helsinki) do not. From 1 Jan 2027 the government proposes restricting it to a parent who cares for the child personally and has 3 years' residence in Finland/EEA.

policies.name: Neuvola, free child healthcare and free school meals
policies.what: Maternity and child health clinics (neuvola) give free pregnancy care and ≈ 15 check-ups by age 6 plus all vaccinations. Public healthcare and dental care are free of client fees for under-18s. Pre-primary education (age 6) and school are free, including a daily hot meal.
policies.value: ≈ 0 € out of pocket for pregnancy, child health, dental and school
policies.eligibility: All residents.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health — child health clinics
policies.caveat: Wellbeing-services-county budgets are tight; waiting times for non-urgent care have grown since 2023.

FR.note: France front-loads support on the under-3s and makes school free from age 3, so this household's expensive years are short. Cash is modest but automatic (allocations familiales from the 2nd child, PAJE base allowance while a child is under 3), maternity pay is near-full, and from July 2026 each parent gets an extra 1-2 months of paid birth leave. The weak spots: a subsidised crèche place is far from guaranteed (roughly one collective place for every five under-3s, long municipal waiting lists), PreParE parental leave pays only about €460/month, and housing benefit (APL) is essentially out of reach at two median wages.

headline.cash: ≈ €350/month (allocations familiales €152 + PAJE base €198) while the baby is under 3, plus a €1,093 birth grant (2026)
headline.leave: 16 weeks maternity at ~full pay, 28 days paternity, plus new 1-2 months per parent at 70%/60% from July 2026
headline.childcare: école maternelle free and compulsory from age 3; crèche fee income-based (~€2.2/hour at median wage) but places scarce
headline.tax: quotient familial (2 kids = 3 parts, cap €1,807/half-part) + 50% tax credit on childcare costs up to €1,750/child/year

policies.name: École maternelle (free from age 3) + income-based crèche fees (barème CNAF/PSU)
policies.what: Public nursery school is free and compulsory from age 3 (24 h/week, lunch extra, income-priced). Before 3, public/PSU crèches charge a national hourly fee: household monthly income x 0.0516% for 2 children, i.e. about €2.20/hour (min €0.41, max €4.39 in 2026-27), so roughly €350-450/month full time.
policies.value: ≈ €0 for the toddler in maternelle; ≈ €400/month for the baby in crèche (before 50% tax credit)
policies.eligibility: All residents; maternelle enrolment via the mairie; crèche places allocated by the commune, working parents prioritised.
policies.caveat: Crèche capacity is the catch: only about 1 collective place per 5 under-3s nationally, waiting lists of months. Fallback is a licensed childminder (assistante maternelle) subsidised via the CMG (complément libre choix du mode de garde, reformed Sept 2025), which costs a median family more than a crèche.

policies.name: Congé maternité, congé paternité and the new congé supplémentaire de naissance
policies.what: Maternity: 16 weeks paid by Sécurité sociale at net salary up to €104/day (2026), i.e. full pay at a median wage. Paternity: 3 days employer-paid + 25 days SS-paid. New from 1 July 2026: each parent gets 1-2 extra months at 70% of net salary the first month and 60% the second (salary counted up to €4,005/month).
policies.value: ≈ 4 months mother + 1 month father near-full pay, plus up to 4 extra months (2 each) at 60-70% for a median-wage couple
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed with recent contribution history; new birth leave open to both parents after maternity/paternity leave is used.
policies.caveat: Beyond this, PreParE parental leave pays only €459.70/month flat (6 months per parent for a first child; up to 24 months each for 2+ children), so long leave means a big income drop.

policies.name: Allocations familiales + PAJE (prime à la naissance, allocation de base)
policies.what: Allocations familiales start from the 2nd child: €152.25/month for 2 children at household income up to €79,980 (2026; halved above, quartered above €106,604). PAJE adds a €1,093 birth grant (2026) and a base allowance of €198.16/month until the child turns 3 (full rate for two-earner couples with 2 children up to €56,478 taxable income).
policies.value: ≈ €350/month while the baby is under 3 (€152 + €198) plus €1,093 at birth; ≈ €152/month afterwards
policies.eligibility: All legal residents; allocations familiales income-modulated but never zero; PAJE base means-tested at a ceiling above two median wages.
policies.caveat: Nothing for a first/only child under allocations familiales. Since March 2026 the age-14 supplement moved to age 18 for new beneficiaries. Rates only rose 0.8% in April 2026.

policies.name: Quotient familial + crédit d'impôt for childcare of under-6s
policies.what: Income tax is computed per 'part': a couple with 2 children has 3 parts instead of 2, capped at €1,807 of tax saving per extra half-part (2025 income, taxed 2026). Separately, 50% of crèche/childminder costs for under-6s is refunded as a tax credit on up to €3,500 of costs per child (max €1,750/child/year), even if no tax is due.
policies.value: ≈ €1,200-1,800/year from the quotient at two median wages + up to €1,750/year credit per child in paid care
policies.eligibility: All taxpayers; joint filing is automatic for married/PACS couples; the childcare credit needs receipts from a licensed carer or crèche.
policies.caveat: At a median wage the quotient saving is limited by the 11% bracket; the childcare credit excludes meals and any CAF subsidy already received.

guide.label: MISSOC — comparative tables on family benefits (EU)

GB.note: For a two-earner renting family the UK's big instrument is now childcare: since September 2025 England funds 30 hours a week from 9 months until school for working parents, plus a 20% Tax-Free Childcare top-up, and Child Benefit is not income-tested until one parent earns £60,000. Everything else is weak: statutory maternity pay drops to a flat £194/week after six weeks, paternity leave is two weeks, there is no family tax relief, and Universal Credit (with its housing and childcare elements) is out of reach at two median wages (median full-time pay £39,039, ASHE April 2025). Figures are for England; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland run different childcare and school-meal schemes (see caveats).

headline.cash: £44.95/week ≈ £2,337/yr (≈ €2,700) Child Benefit for 2 kids (2026/27), no means test below £60k per parent
headline.leave: 39 weeks paid maternity: 6 weeks at 90% then £194.32/week; 2 weeks paternity at £194.32
headline.childcare: 30 funded hours/week from 9 months to school (38 weeks/yr) for working parents; +20% Tax-Free Childcare top-up
headline.tax: no family tax splitting or child tax credit; Tax-Free Childcare adds up to £2,000/child/yr

policies.name: 30 hours funded childcare for working parents (England, 9 months to school age)
policies.what: Since 1 September 2025 eligible working parents in England get 30 hours a week of government-funded childcare for 38 weeks a year (can be stretched over 52) from the term after the child turns 9 months until they start school. Each parent must earn at least 16 hours a week at the National Living Wage (£2,643.68 per 3 months, ≈ £203/week) and neither may have adjusted net income over £100,000. All 3–4-year-olds get 15 hours regardless of work.
policies.value: ≈ 1,140 funded hours per child per year, worth roughly £7,000–£10,000 (≈ €8,000–11,500) per child at typical nursery fees
policies.eligibility: Both parents working and earning ≥ £2,643.68 per 3 months, each under £100,000 adjusted net income; reconfirm every 3 months via the childcare service.
policies.url_label: GOV.UK — Free childcare if you're working
policies.caveat: Providers may charge for meals, nappies and 'consumables' and for hours beyond 30; baby-room places are scarce in many areas; funding stops in school holidays unless stretched. Scotland (1,140 hours from age 3), Wales (Flying Start/Childcare Offer) and Northern Ireland (subsidy scheme) differ.

policies.name: Child Benefit
policies.what: Universal weekly benefit paid 4-weekly by HMRC: £27.05 for the eldest child and £17.90 for each additional child from 6 April 2026 (up 3.8%). Not means-tested unless one parent's adjusted net income exceeds £60,000; then the High Income Child Benefit Charge claws back 1% per £200, fully withdrawn at £80,000. Claiming also protects the carer's State Pension record.
policies.value: £44.95/week = £2,337/yr (≈ €2,700) for 2 children
policies.eligibility: Anyone responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 in education) living in the UK; charge applies only if either parent earns over £60,000.
policies.caveat: The £60,000 test is per individual, not per household: two parents on £59,000 each keep it all, one on £80,000 loses it all. Rates are UK-wide.

policies.name: Tax-Free Childcare
policies.what: For every £8 a working family pays into an online childcare account the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year (£4,000 if disabled) for children under 12, spendable at any registered nursery, childminder, club or nanny. Works alongside the 30 funded hours to cover the remaining hours, extras and school-holiday care.
policies.value: up to £2,000/child/yr (≈ €2,300), i.e. up to £4,000 for 2 children
policies.eligibility: Same work and income test as the funded hours: each parent earns ≥ 16 hours at minimum wage and < £100,000; cannot be combined with Universal Credit childcare or childcare vouchers.
policies.caveat: You only get the full £2,000 if you spend £10,000 of your own money per child; eligibility must be reconfirmed every 3 months. UK-wide scheme.

policies.name: Statutory Maternity Pay, Paternity Pay and Shared Parental Leave
policies.what: Mothers can take 52 weeks' leave; Statutory Maternity Pay runs 39 weeks: 6 weeks at 90% of average earnings, then 33 weeks at £194.32/week (2026/27) or 90% if lower. Fathers get 2 weeks' paternity leave at £194.32 — a day-one right since 6 April 2026 under the Employment Rights Act 2025 (pay still needs 26 weeks' service). Parents may convert up to 50 weeks into Shared Parental Leave (37 paid weeks at the flat rate). Unpaid parental leave: 18 weeks per child.
policies.value: ≈ £10,500 (≈ €12,000) over 9 months for a mother on £39,000, i.e. ~36% of pay; ≈ £390 for the father's 2 weeks
policies.eligibility: Employees with 26 weeks' continuous service by the 15th week before the due date and earnings ≥ £129/week; self-employed mothers get Maternity Allowance instead.
policies.caveat: The flat rate is about a quarter of median full-time pay; employer top-ups are common in large firms but voluntary. Neonatal care leave (up to 12 weeks) added in April 2025.

policies.name: Free NHS care for children + universal infant free school meals (England)
policies.what: All NHS treatment is free; prescriptions are free under 16, NHS dental care free under 18, eye tests free under 16, and the health-visitor programme covers checks to age 2.5. Every Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 pupil in an English state school gets a free lunch (Universal Infant Free School Meals); from September 2026 all children in Universal Credit households qualify at every age.
policies.value: ≈ £500/yr (≈ €575) per child in infant school in meals, plus no out-of-pocket child health costs
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the UK (NHS); all pupils in Reception–Year 2 in England (UIFSM); low-income families also get Healthy Start vouchers.
policies.url_label: GOV.UK — Universal infant free school meals 2026 to 2027
policies.caveat: Scotland and Wales give free primary-school meals to all ages; NHS dental capacity is poor in many areas even though the entitlement is free. No housing support exists at this income: Universal Credit's housing element is out of reach and the Lifetime ISA first-home bonus needs your own savings.

guide.label: GOV.UK — Childcare and parenting overview

GR.note: Greece pays a lot up front (a tiered birth grant, then 9 months of state-paid maternity leave at minimum wage) and has cut income tax for parents from 2026, but ongoing cash is thin: the means-tested A21 child benefit (equivalent income ≤ €15,000) is out of reach for two full-time median earners (≈ €32,000–35,000 gross combined). Childcare for under-4s depends on annual EU-funded vouchers and scarce municipal places; only public kindergarten from age 4 is free and guaranteed. Renting gets a modest new rent refund; wages are low and Athens rents high.

headline.cash: birth grant €2,400 for the 1st child, €2,700 for the 2nd (2026); A21 child benefit only if one parent works less
headline.leave: 17 weeks maternity at ~full pay, then 9 months at minimum wage (€920/month); 14 days paternity; 2 paid months parental leave per parent
headline.childcare: ESPA voucher ≈ €2,000–2,800/yr per child for families under €35,000; free public kindergarten from age 4
headline.tax: 2026 family tax scale: 16% instead of 20% on €10–20k with 2 kids, credit €1,120; extra cut if a parent is under 30

policies.name: Maternity leave + 9-month special maternity protection leave (DYPA) + paternity/parental leave
policies.what: Private-sector mothers get 17 weeks (119 days) maternity leave paid by EFKA plus a DYPA supplement so pay is roughly maintained, then up to 9 months 'special maternity protection leave' paid by DYPA at the statutory minimum wage (€920 gross/month from April 2026; extended from 6 to 9 months in 2023). Fathers: 14 working days paid paternity leave. Parental leave 4 months per parent, first 2 months paid by DYPA at minimum wage.
policies.value: ≈ €8,300 (9 × €920) per birth after ~4 months of near-full pay; + ≈ €1,840 per parent for 2 paid parental-leave months
policies.eligibility: Employees insured with EFKA (self-employed mothers covered since 2024); parental-leave pay needs 1 year with the employer.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Labour — 9-month special maternity leave (clarifications)
policies.caveat: The 9 months are paid at minimum wage, not salary; the father's 14 days are paid by the employer; public-sector rules differ. Applications run through the DYPA parental-benefits portal.

policies.name: Birth grant (Επίδομα γέννησης, OPEKA)
policies.what: One-off grant for every child born in Greece, tiered since 1 January 2026: €2,400 for the first child, €2,700 for the second, €3,000 for the third, €3,500 for the fourth or later (was a flat €2,000 in 2020–2023, €2,400 in 2024–25). Paid in two equal instalments, the first the month after birth. Applied for by the mother online.
policies.value: €5,100 one-off for a first and a second child (2026 rates)
policies.eligibility: Equivalent family income ≤ €40,000/year; mother legally and permanently resident in Greece.
policies.caveat: The recurring A21 child benefit (€70/€42/€28 per child per month by equivalent income ≤ €6,000/€10,000/€15,000; scale 1 + 0.5 partner + 0.25 per child) is not payable at two median wages: €33,000 ÷ 2.0 = €16,500 equivalent income. If one parent goes part-time the family may drop into category C and get about €56/month for 2 kids.

policies.name: ESPA childcare vouchers (EETAA) + free public kindergarten from 4
policies.what: Each summer EETAA allocates EU co-funded vouchers ('Harmonisation of family and professional life') that cover fees at public or private infant-toddler centres for children from 2 months to 4 years; income limit for 2025/26 and 2026/27 is €35,000 gross for families with up to 2 children. Public kindergarten (nipiagogeio) is compulsory and free for two years from age 4.
policies.value: roughly €2,000–2,800/yr per child in fees covered (2026/27 call); €0 for kindergarten from age 4
policies.eligibility: Family income ≤ €35,000 (2 children); working, self-employed or job-seeking parents; ranked by points (income, single parent, disability).
policies.caveat: A dual-median-income family sits right at the €35,000 ceiling and low on the points list; municipal nurseries are oversubscribed in Athens and private fees often exceed the voucher. The exact voucher amounts change with each annual call.

policies.name: 2026 family income-tax scale + child tax credit
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 the rate on income of €10,001–20,000 is 20% with no children, 18% with one, 16% with two, 9% with three and 0% with four or more; on €20,001–30,000 it is 26/24/22/20/18%. The tax credit is €777 with no children, €900 with one and €1,120 with two. Workers under 25 pay 0% up to €20,000; those aged 26–30 pay 9% on €10,001–20,000.
policies.value: roughly €600/yr less tax per parent at €20,000 (≈ €1,200 per household); several hundred euros more if a parent is under 30
policies.eligibility: Every taxpayer with dependent children; the reduced rates and credits are applied per parent in the annual return.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Economy & Finance — Income taxation (2026 scale)
policies.caveat: Savings are small at Greek wage levels because most of the income sits in the 9% first bracket; the tax credit cannot turn negative, so a low earner gains little.

policies.name: Annual rent refund (Επιστροφή ενοικίου, AADE)
policies.what: Since November 2025 tenants get one month's rent back every November, paid automatically by the tax authority (AADE) from the rent declared in their tax return. Cap €800 for the main residence plus €50 per dependent child (€900 with 2 children). Income limits for the November 2026 payment: €35,000 for a couple plus €5,000 per child (€45,000 with 2 kids); property-wealth cap €120,000 plus €20,000 per family member.
policies.value: ≈ €900/yr (one month's rent, capped) for a renting couple with 2 children
policies.eligibility: Tenants whose lease is declared electronically to AADE and who file a tax return on time; income and property caps as above; nationwide.
policies.url_label: Ministry of National Economy & Finance (scheme owner; paid via AADE/myAADE)
policies.caveat: Regular housing benefit (Επίδομα στέγασης) is not reachable at median income. Regional public-sector doctors, nurses and teachers get two months instead of one. The state's 'Σπίτι μου II' cheap-mortgage scheme (ages 25–50) still needs a bank deposit.

HR.note: Since the March 2025 reform Croatia is strong on leave: about 14 months at full pay per child (maternity uncapped, parental capped at €3,000/month) plus 20 working days of paid paternity, a €618 birth grant and a real child tax allowance. Cash child allowance is means-tested below what a two-earner couple earns, so it does not reach this household. Childcare is municipal: cheap or free in Zagreb and many towns but with waiting lists and no legal entitlement to a place; housing support for renters is practically nil.

headline.cash: €618.02 one-off per newborn; monthly child allowance (€31-62/child) only if net income ≤ €618/household member
headline.leave: 6 months maternity at 100% uncapped + 8 months parental at 100% (cap €3,001.79/month), 2 months per parent non-transferable; 20 working days paternity at 100%
headline.childcare: municipal kindergarten: Zagreb most parents pay €0-40/month, elsewhere up to ~€170; no guaranteed place
headline.tax: monthly tax-free allowance +€300 (1st) +€420 (2nd child) → ≈ €1,700-2,000/year less income tax

policies.name: Rodiljni i roditeljski dopust (maternity and parental leave)
policies.what: Maternity leave from 28 days before birth until the child is 6 months old at 100% of pay with no cap, paid by HZZO. Then parental leave of 8 months for a 1st or 2nd child (4 months per parent, 2 of them non-transferable) at 100% of pay capped at €3,001.79/month (680% of the budget base, since 1 March 2025; before that €995). Minimum €701.89/month.
policies.value: ≈ 14 months at full net pay per child for a parent on a median net wage of roughly €1,300 (cap of €3,001.79 is well above it)
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed parent with 12 months of continuous (or 18 of 24 months) health insurance; otherwise a flat €701.89/month.
policies.url_label: HZZO (Croatian Health Insurance Fund) — Rodiljne i roditeljske potpore
policies.caveat: The 2-month non-transferable father's share is lost if he does not use it; leave can be used until the child is 8 but at a lower flat rate after the first year.

policies.name: Uvećani osobni odbitak za djecu (child personal tax allowance)
policies.what: The basic tax-free monthly allowance of €600 is increased by €300 for the 1st child (coefficient 0.5), €420 for the 2nd (0.7) and €600 for the 3rd (1.0) (2025-2026). One parent claims each child, or parents split. Income tax rates are set by the municipality (about 20-23% lower rate in 2026, 30-33% above €5,000/month).
policies.value: ≈ €720/month extra tax-free income for 2 children → roughly €145-165/month (€1,700-2,000/year) more net pay at a median wage
policies.eligibility: Any resident taxpayer supporting a child whose own income is under €3,600/year; registered on the PK tax card via the employer.
policies.caveat: Only reduces tax actually due: a low-paid parent with a €600 basic allowance already pays little tax, so the higher earner should claim both children. No increase of the allowance in 2026.

policies.name: Očinski dopust (paternity leave)
policies.what: Fathers get 20 working days of paid paternity leave for one child (30 for twins) to be used in the first 6 months, at 100% of pay with no cap, funded from the state budget and paid by HZZO. Doubled from 10 days on 1 March 2025. Independent of the mother's leave.
policies.value: 4 fully paid weeks per child for the father, ≈ €1,300 net at a median wage, on top of his 2+ months of parental leave
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed father with health insurance; must be used within 6 months of birth.

policies.name: Jednokratna novčana potpora za novorođeno dijete (birth grant)
policies.what: One-off state payment of €618.02 per newborn (140% of the budget base), doubled from €309 on 1 March 2025, claimed from HZZO within 6 months of birth. Most cities and counties pay their own additional newborn grants (typically €300-1,300; Zagreb and coastal towns higher), and Zagreb co-finances private kindergartens.
policies.value: €1,236 from the state for two births, plus a municipal grant of a few hundred euros each in most towns
policies.eligibility: Croatian citizen or permanent resident with health insurance; no income test.
policies.url_label: gov.hr — Novčana potpora za novorođeno dijete
policies.caveat: The monthly child allowance (doplatak za djecu, €30.90-61.80 per child) is paid only if net income per household member is at most €618.02/month, so a two-median-wage couple with 2 children usually does not qualify.

policies.name: Sufinancirani gradski vrtići + besplatni školski obroci (subsidised municipal kindergarten, free school meals)
policies.what: Kindergartens (from 1 year) are run and priced by municipalities. In Zagreb the parent fee is income-based: about a third of parents pay €0-20/month and most under €40 against an economic price of ~€340; 17 towns charge nothing, others up to ~€170/month. The pre-school year is free. Since 2023/24 the state pays €1.33 per school meal for every primary-school pupil, and primary textbooks are state-funded.
policies.value: ≈ €0-80/month for a 3-year-old in a city kindergarten (Zagreb ≈ €0-40); free meals and textbooks once in primary school
policies.eligibility: Residence in the municipality; both parents employed usually gives priority; no legal entitlement to a place.
policies.caveat: Waiting lists in Zagreb, Split and the coast are long for under-3s; private kindergartens cost €300-500/month (Zagreb subsidises them by ~€400). Fees and capacity vary enormously by municipality.
