HU.note: Hungary channels most support through the tax system, which suits a dual-earner household: the doubled family tax allowance (80,000 HUF/month for two children) plus, from January 2026, a lifelong 0% income tax for mothers under 40 with two children, and tax-free earnings-related leave (CSED 100% for 6 months, GYED 70% to age 2). Flat cash benefits are weak — the universal családi pótlék has been frozen at 12,200–16,000 HUF per child since 2008. Kindergarten is free and guaranteed from age 3; crèche places for under-3s are uneven outside cities. Housing schemes (Otthon Start 3% loan, CSOK Plusz) need a 10% deposit or a mortgage; only the Babaváró loan is reachable without savings.

headline.cash: családi pótlék 26,600 HUF/month (≈ €67) for 2 kids, frozen since 2008; Babaváró 11m HUF (≈ €28k) interest-free loan, 30% forgiven at 2nd child
headline.leave: CSED 100% of pay for 24 weeks, then GYED 70% (cap 451,920 HUF/month, 2026) until age 2 — both tax-free; father may take GYED
headline.childcare: óvoda free and guaranteed from age 3 (compulsory); crèche fee ≤ 25% of per-capita income; free meals below ~279,000 HUF per-capita net income
headline.tax: family tax allowance 40,000 HUF per child per month with 2 kids (≈ €200/month) + 0% PIT for mothers of two under 40 from 2026

policies.name: Családi (adó)kedvezmény — family tax allowance
policies.what: Reduces income tax by 20,000 HUF/month with one child, 40,000 HUF per child with two, 66,000 HUF per child with three or more (2026, after doubling in 2025–26). Any part not usable against the 15% PIT is deducted from the 18.5% social-security contribution. Parents may split it; counts from the 91st day of pregnancy.
policies.value: 80,000 HUF/month (≈ €200), i.e. ≈ 960,000 HUF/year, for two children — typically claimed by the father while the mother is PIT-exempt
policies.eligibility: Parents entitled to családi pótlék for the child (all residents); needs taxable earned income or contributions to offset.
policies.caveat: Worth the full amount only if the claiming parent's PIT + contributions reach 80,000 HUF/month (gross ≈ 240,000 HUF) — fine at a median wage, not while on GYES.

policies.name: CSED + GYED (earnings-related maternity and childcare benefit)
policies.what: CSED: 100% of average daily gross earnings for 168 days (24 weeks) from birth. GYED: from day 169 until the child's 2nd birthday, 70% of previous earnings, capped at 70% of twice the minimum wage — 451,920 HUF/month in 2026. Both PIT-exempt since July 2025, so net pay can exceed the previous salary. Father may take GYED; the parent may work without limit once the child is 6 months old. Then GYES 28,500 HUF/month to age 3.
policies.value: ≈ 520,000 HUF/month (≈ €1,300) tax-free for 6 months, then ≈ 365,000 HUF/month (≈ €920) for 18 months at a median wage
policies.eligibility: 365 days of insurance (employment) in the 2 years before birth; GYED also for the father.
policies.caveat: Uninsured parents get only the flat GYES (28,500 HUF/month); the GYED cap bites above ~645,000 HUF gross.

policies.name: Kétgyermekes anyák szja-mentessége — 0% income tax for mothers of two
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 mothers under 40 who raise (or raised for 12+ years) two children pay no personal income tax on any earned income — wages, self-employment, commissions — for life, with no cap. Phased in by age: under 40 in 2026, under 50 from 2027, under 60 from 2028, all from 2029. Claimed via a tax-advance declaration to the employer.
policies.value: ≈ 78,000 HUF/month (≈ €200), i.e. 15% of gross, for a mother on a median wage (~520,000 HUF)
policies.eligibility: Mothers with at least two children who are (or were for 12 years) entitled to családi pótlék; in 2026 only those born after 31 December 1985.
policies.caveat: Applies only to the mother's earned income (not capital or rental income); contributions (18.5%) are still due. Mothers of three or more have been exempt since 2019.

policies.name: Babaváró támogatás — 11 million HUF interest-free loan
policies.what: Unsecured bank loan of up to 11 million HUF (≈ €28,000) for married couples where the wife is aged 18–35, repayable over up to 20 years (max 51,000 HUF/month), interest-free if a child is born within 5 years. Repayment is suspended 3 years per child; 30% of the debt is written off at the second child and all of it at the third. Usable for a rental deposit, furnishing or a home purchase.
policies.value: ≈ 3.3 million HUF (≈ €8,400) forgiven with two children plus an interest-free 11m HUF loan (0.5%/year guarantee fee)
policies.eligibility: Married couple, wife 18–35, one spouse with 3 years of social insurance, clean credit record.
policies.caveat: If no child arrives within 5 years the loan becomes market-rate and the interest subsidy must be repaid. The 3% fixed Otthon Start mortgage (up to 50m HUF, from Sept 2025) is the main first-home scheme but needs a 10% deposit.

policies.name: Free óvoda from age 3, subsidised bölcsőde, free meals
policies.what: Kindergarten (óvoda) is compulsory and free of charge from the September after the child turns 3, with a guaranteed place; only meals are charged. Crèches (bölcsőde, 0–3) may charge a care fee of at most 25% of per-capita net family income — many municipalities charge nothing. Meals in both are free for families with per-capita net income below 130% of the net minimum wage (≈ 279,000 HUF in 2026) or with 3+ children. Textbooks and child healthcare are free.
policies.value: Full-day kindergarten for roughly 0–15,000 HUF/month in meals per child; free meals reachable for a two-earner median family with two kids
policies.eligibility: All resident children; meal exemption by declaration to the institution.
policies.caveat: Bölcsőde coverage is patchy in small towns and villages (many have none), and waiting lists are common in Budapest; private crèches cost 150,000–250,000 HUF/month.

official.label: csalad.hu — government family-support portal

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Hungary

IE.note: Ireland's support for a working couple is universal but thin: €140/month per child, flat-rate €299/week leave that replaces less than half a median wage, and a childcare subsidy that at two median incomes falls back to the universal €2.14/hour, leaving full-time crèche bills of roughly €180-200/week per child even under the fee cap. The strong points are free pre-school (ECCE) for two years from age 2 years 8 months, free GP care under 8, free primary schoolbooks and hot school meals, and generous employer-independent leave weeks. Rent is the biggest unaddressed cost: housing supports (HAP) are not available at this income; only the €1,000 renter tax credit and the Help to Buy scheme for a first new-build home apply.

headline.cash: €280/month for 2 kids (Child Benefit €140/child, unchanged in Budget 2026)
headline.leave: 26 weeks maternity + 2 weeks paternity + 9 weeks per parent, all at a flat €299/week (2026)
headline.childcare: NCS universal subsidy €2.14/hour (≈ €96/week/child); income-assessed up to €5.10/hour below €68k net income; fee cap €295/week
headline.healthedu: ECCE: 15 hours/week free pre-school for 2 years; free GP visits under 8; free primary schoolbooks and hot school meals

policies.name: National Childcare Scheme (NCS) + core-funding fee cap
policies.what: Government pays part of the crèche bill directly to the provider. Universal subsidy (no means test): €2.14/hour for up to 45 hours/week per child. Income-assessed subsidy from 31 Aug 2026: up to €5.10/hour at net family income ≤ €34,000, tapering to zero at €68,000, after a €5,500 discount for 2 children. Core-funded services must cap fees at €295/week (2025-26).
policies.value: ≈ €96/week per child (≈ €830/month for 2 in full-time care) at two median wages; parents still pay ≈ €180-200/week per child
policies.eligibility: Children 24 weeks to 15 years in a Tusla-registered, NCS-contracted service; 45 subsidised hours need both parents working/studying.
policies.caveat: At two median wages net income sits at or above the €68,000 cut-off, so only the universal rate applies. Places are scarce (waiting lists from pregnancy in Dublin) and Irish fees remain among the EU's highest. A lower fee cap (about €280/week for 45 hours) was announced for services from September 2026.

policies.name: Maternity Benefit, Paternity Benefit and Parent's Benefit
policies.what: Maternity leave: 26 weeks with Maternity Benefit of €299/week (from Jan 2026) plus 16 unpaid weeks. Paternity leave: 2 weeks at €299/week. Parent's leave: 9 weeks per parent, non-transferable, in the child's first 2 years, at €299/week. All paid by the Department of Social Protection on PRSI record; employers may top up but need not.
policies.value: ≈ €13,150 per birth from the state (26 + 2 + 9 + 9 weeks x €299) — under half of a median wage while on leave
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed with 39+ PRSI weeks in the relevant period; leave itself is a statutory right for all employees.
policies.caveat: Flat rate, not earnings-related: a median earner (~€45,000) loses roughly half of net pay each week on leave unless the employer tops up, which many small employers do not.

policies.name: Child Benefit
policies.what: Universal monthly payment of €140 per child, paid on the first Tuesday of the month to the parent, tax-free and not means-tested, until 16 (or 19 in education). Rate was not changed in Budget 2026; a means-tested second tier for low-income families is planned but not yet introduced.
policies.value: €280/month (€3,360/year) for 2 children
policies.eligibility: All children ordinarily resident in Ireland; automatic registration at birth for Irish-born children.
policies.caveat: Frozen at €140 since 2016 apart from one-off double payments; real value has eroded. The Child Support Payment increases in Budget 2026 apply only to families on welfare payments.

policies.name: ECCE free pre-school + free GP care under 8 + free primary schoolbooks and hot school meals
policies.what: ECCE: 3 hours/day, 5 days/week, 38 weeks/year of free pre-school for 2 years, from the September after a child turns 2 years 8 months. GP visit card: free GP visits and assessments for every child under 8, no means test. Primary school: free schoolbooks and workbooks (since 2023) and hot school meals in all primary schools eligible from 2025.
policies.value: ≈ €70/week per child in ECCE (state pays the provider) + ≈ €60-70 per avoided GP visit + ≈ €100-150/year books/meals per primary pupil
policies.eligibility: Universal for resident children; ECCE via any participating pre-school; GP card via HSE registration.
policies.caveat: ECCE covers only 15 hours/week in term time; working parents still pay for wrap-around hours (NCS-subsidised). Free GP care ends at 8; prescriptions and hospital A&E charges still apply.

official.label: gov.ie — Department of Social Protection Budget 2026 measures

guide.label: Citizens Information — Budget 2026 (family, childcare, housing)

IS.note: Iceland pays 12 months of parental leave at 80% of wages (cap raised to 900,000 ISK/month in 2026) and, in Reykjavík, preschool is now free for the first 36 hours a week. The famous weakness is the 'care gap': municipal preschool places usually start around 18 months, six months after leave ends, and rents are very high. The income-tested child benefit (barnabætur) is largely phased out at two median wages and the housing benefit is out of reach for them; there is no family taxation.

headline.cash: ≈ 340,000 ISK/year (≈ €2,350) barnabætur for 2 children at two median wages — the under-7 supplement is fully phased out
headline.leave: 12 months total (6 per parent, 6 weeks transferable) at 80% of wage, max 900,000 ISK/month (2026)
headline.childcare: Reykjavík: first 36 h/week free since April 2026; 8 h/day ≈ 33,300 ISK/month incl. meals — but places typically only from ≈ 18 months
headline.tax: none: only the personal tax credit is transferable between spouses

policies.name: Fæðingarorlof (parental leave from the Maternity/Paternity Leave Fund)
policies.what: 12 months of paid leave per birth: 6 months for each parent, of which up to 6 weeks can be transferred to the other. Payment is 80% of average total earnings over the reference period, capped at 900,000 ISK/month for leave taken from 1 Jan 2026 (800,000 in 2025); minimum 275,688 ISK for 50–100% jobs. Must be used before the child turns 2.
policies.value: ≈ 680,000 ISK/month (≈ €4,700) at an 850,000 ISK median wage, for 6 months each parent
policies.eligibility: Worked continuously in Iceland for 6 months before the birth at ≥ 25%; others get a flat parental grant (fæðingarstyrkur).
policies.caveat: Cap means higher earners lose more; the 6 weeks transferable are lost if the other parent does not use their months.

policies.name: Leikskóli (municipal preschool) — Reykjavík fee schedule
policies.what: Reykjavík (≈ 1/3 of the population; other municipalities similar) charges no tuition for the first 36 h/week from 1 April 2026; an 8-hour day costs 18,000 ISK tuition + 15,290 ISK meals ≈ 33,300 ISK/month, less 20–40% discounts below 18 / 11 million ISK household income; older siblings with the same hours pay no tuition. Children are ranked by age; the city aims to offer places to children who are 18 months by 1 September.
policies.value: ≈ 33,300 ISK/month (≈ €230) for a full 8-hour place incl. meals for the toddler; the baby will likely wait until ≈ 18 months
policies.eligibility: Children registered in Reykjavík, waiting list from 6 months; earliest start 12 months for priority cases.
policies.caveat: The gap between 12-month leave and an 18–24-month place must be bridged with subsidised childminders (dagforeldrar, often 100,000+ ISK/month net) or unpaid time; staff shortages cause closures.

policies.name: Barnabætur (income-tested child benefit)
policies.what: Paid via the tax system in four instalments. 2026: 345,000 ISK per child per year for couples (514,500 for single parents) plus 130,000 ISK per child under 7. Reduced by 4% of the couple's joint income above 11,688,000 ISK/year; the under-7 supplement is reduced separately by 4% per child, so it disappears quickly.
policies.value: ≈ 340,000 ISK/year (≈ €2,350, ≈ 28,000 ISK/month) for two children at ≈ 20.4 million ISK joint income; zero above ≈ 29 million ISK
policies.eligibility: Tax-resident parents of children under 18; assessed on the previous year's tax return.
policies.caveat: Heavily income-tested: worth much more to below-median households; amounts unchanged from 2025 in nominal terms.

policies.name: Free child healthcare, well-baby care and dental care
policies.what: Children under 2 pay nothing for public healthcare; from 2 to 18 care is free at the health centre and with a referral, with a monthly out-of-pocket cap of 25,198 ISK otherwise (2026). Ungbarnavernd (well-baby clinic) check-ups and vaccinations are free. Dental care for children is fully covered by Sjúkratryggingar except one 2,500 ISK annual fee (register with a family dentist).
policies.value: ≈ 0–2,500 ISK/year out of pocket for child health and dental
policies.eligibility: All children insured in Iceland (6 months' residence).
policies.caveat: Orthodontics is only partly subsidised; GP appointments in the capital area can take weeks.

official.label: Ísland.is — Having a baby (life-event guide, English)

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EEA social protection)

IT.note: Italy's support is cash-heavy and ISEE-tested: the Assegno Unico is paid to every family but its size depends on the ISEE indicator, which for a renting two-earner couple with two small children usually lands in the middle-to-upper band. Nursery costs are cushioned by the Bonus Nido (up to €3,600/yr) but public nido places cover only about a third of under-3s and far fewer in the South. Leave is decent for mothers (5 months at 80%) but paternity is 10 days and most shared parental leave is paid at 30%; preschool from 3 is free.

headline.cash: Assegno Unico ≈ €400–580/month for a newborn + toddler at ISEE €15–25k (2026), min ≈ €120/month above ISEE €46.6k; €1,000 birth bonus
headline.leave: 5 months maternity at 80% + 10 days paternity at 100%; 3 shared months at 80% (rest of 10–11 months at 30%)
headline.childcare: Bonus Nido up to €3,600/yr per child under 3 (ISEE ≤ €40k); free state scuola dell'infanzia 3–6, but nido places scarce
headline.tax: no child tax credit for under-21s since 2022 (folded into Assegno Unico); working mothers of 2+ get €60/month bonus mamme

policies.name: Assegno Unico e Universale (AUU)
policies.what: Monthly benefit per child from the 7th month of pregnancy to 21 (no limit for disabled). 2026: €203.80 per child at ISEE ≤ €17,468.51, tapering to €58.30 at ISEE ≥ €46,582.71 or without ISEE. Add-ons: +50% for each child under 1; up to +€34.90 per child when both parents work; +€34.90 for 3+ children. Tax-free, paid by INPS.
policies.value: roughly €400–580/month for a newborn + toddler at ISEE €15–25k (typical for renting two-earner families); ≈ €120/month with no ISEE
policies.eligibility: Residents (EU citizens or 2-year residence permit), Italian tax residence; apply once to INPS, renew ISEE each year by 28 Feb.
policies.url_label: INPS — Assegno unico e universale per i figli a carico
policies.caveat: ISEE counts income AND assets (20%) with a rent deduction up to ~€7,000, so savings or a modest inheritance shrink the benefit; without a valid ISEE you get the minimum only.

policies.name: Bonus asilo nido + free scuola dell'infanzia 3–6
policies.what: INPS reimburses nursery fees (public or licensed private) for children under 3: up to €3,600/yr (11 monthly instalments) for children born from 2024 with ISEE ≤ €40,000; €1,500/yr above €40,000 or without ISEE. From 2026 one application lasts until the child turns 3. From age 3 state scuola dell'infanzia is free (meals charged, income-scaled).
policies.value: ≈ €300/month per child in nursery (up to €7,200/yr for two under-3s); then ≈ €4,000–6,000/yr saved per child from 3 in a free state preschool
policies.eligibility: Child under 3 enrolled in a nido; parent applies online to INPS with receipts; ISEE minorenni.
policies.caveat: Bonus cannot exceed fees actually paid and is paid in arrears; public nido coverage is ~30% of under-3s nationally (under 15% in parts of the South), so many families pay €400–700/month privately and wait for the refund.

policies.name: Congedo di maternità, paternità obbligatorio e congedo parentale
policies.what: Mother: 5 months compulsory maternity leave at 80% of pay (many collective agreements top up to 100%). Father: 10 working days at 100%. Then up to 10 shared months of parental leave (11 if the father takes 3+), usable to age 14: since 2025 three of the couple's months are paid at 80% if taken before age 6, rest 30%.
policies.value: ≈ 5.5 months of near-full pay for the mother per birth + 3 months at 80% shared; further months cost 70% of one salary
policies.eligibility: Employees registered with INPS (self-employed and gig workers have reduced versions).
policies.url_label: INPS — Indennità di congedo parentale per lavoratori dipendenti
policies.caveat: The 80% months are shared between parents, not per parent; parental leave at 30% is rarely affordable, so fathers take little of it.

policies.name: Bonus nuovi nati (€1,000 birth bonus) + Bonus mamme lavoratrici
policies.what: One-off €1,000 from INPS for every child born or adopted from 1 Jan 2025 in families with ISEE ≤ €40,000 (confirmed for 2026). Separately, employed mothers with at least 2 children and income ≤ €40,000 get a tax-free 'bonus mamme' of €60/month (€720/yr) in 2026, until the younger child turns 10.
policies.value: ≈ €1,000 per birth + €720/yr for the mother while she has two children under 10
policies.eligibility: ISEE ≤ €40,000 (nuovi nati); employed/self-employed mothers of 2+ children with income ≤ €40,000 (bonus mamme).
policies.caveat: Both are recent (2025) and budget-dependent; the birth bonus must be claimed within 60 days of birth, and the bonus mamme was €40/month in 2025 and paid in a lump sum in December.

official.label: INPS — Assegno unico e universale (portal)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Italy

LT.note: Lithuania combines a long, well-paid leave (maternity 77.58% uncapped, then 60% of pay until the child is 18 months, with 2 months reserved per parent) with a universal 'child money' payment of €129.50 per child and a €1,036 birth grant from June 2026. A municipal kindergarten place is guaranteed by law from age 2 since 2025 and costs only tens of euros a month in Vilnius. There are no child tax credits (replaced by child money in 2018) and no rent support at median wage; the generous 20–25% first-home subsidy for young families is only available outside the big cities and is rationed by budget.

headline.cash: €259/month for 2 kids (child money €129.50 each) + €1,036 birth grant from June 2026
headline.leave: maternity 126 days at 77.58% uncapped; 30 days paternity; 2 non-transferable months each at 77.58%, then 60% until child is 18 months (or 45%/30% to 24 months)
headline.childcare: municipal kindergarten place guaranteed from age 2 (since 2025); Vilnius fee €26/month + meals ≈ €3–4/day; pre-primary and grades 1–2 meals free
headline.tax: none — child tax allowances were replaced by universal child money in 2018

policies.name: Maternity, paternity and child-care benefit (Sodra)
policies.what: Maternity: 126 days (70 before, 56 after) at 77.58% of insured pay, no ceiling. Paternity: 30 days at 77.58%. Child-care benefit: each parent 2 non-transferable months at 77.58% (max €3,768/month Q1 2026), then 60% until the child is 18 months, or 45% for 12 months then 30% to 24 months. Ceiling 2x average wage (≈ €4,831), floor €560–592.
policies.value: ≈ €1,475/month during maternity and the reserved months, then ≈ €1,140/month at a €1,900 gross wage; roughly €22,000 gross per child over 18 months
policies.eligibility: 12 months of social insurance in the last 24 months; both parents must be insured to use both non-transferable blocks.
policies.caveat: Duration option is fixed once chosen. Earnings while on child-care leave reduce the benefit (except in the non-transferable months). Uninsured parents get a flat €444/month until age 2 from June 2026.

policies.name: Child money (išmoka vaikui) + one-off childbirth grant
policies.what: Universal, non-means-tested €129.50/month per child (1.75 x basic social benefit of €74, 2026) from birth to 18 (23 if in school). An extra €76.22/month per child only for families with 3+ children, a disabled child or income under €352/person. One-off grant per newborn: €814, rising to 14 basic social benefits = €1,036 for births from 1 June 2026.
policies.value: €259/month for 2 kids (€3,108/year) plus €1,036 per birth from June 2026
policies.eligibility: All children permanently resident in Lithuania; apply once via spis.lt or the municipality.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Social Security and Labour — benefits for children
policies.caveat: A two-earner median family does not qualify for the €76 supplement. Indexed only through the basic social benefit (€70 → €74 in 2026).

policies.name: Guaranteed municipal kindergarten place from age 2, low fees
policies.what: Since 2025 the Education Law obliges municipalities to provide an early-education place for every child from age 2 (phased in from age 4 in 2023). Vilnius municipal kindergartens charge a €26/month education fee (€13 for social-benefit recipients) plus meals of roughly €3–4 per attended day. One year of pre-primary is compulsory from the year the child turns 6 (5 allowed) with free meals.
policies.value: ≈ €90–110/month per child in Vilnius (fee + meals), two kids ≈ €200/month
policies.eligibility: Children registered in the municipality; admission via the municipal e-system (Vilnius: darželiai.vilnius.lt).
policies.url_label: Eurydice — early childhood education and care in Lithuania
policies.caveat: The guarantee is a place somewhere in the municipality, not in the preferred kindergarten; Vilnius and Kaunas suburbs still have queues for 1–2 year olds. Fees differ by municipality.

policies.name: Financial incentive for young families buying a first home
policies.what: State subsidy paid to the bank against a first-home mortgage for families where both spouses (or the single parent) are under 36: 15% of the loan with no children, 20% with one child, 25% with two, 30% with three or more, calculated on a loan of up to €87,000. Can be used as the down payment. Not available in the largest cities and their neighbouring municipalities.
policies.value: Up to €21,750 (25% of an €87,000 loan) for a 2-child family buying outside Vilnius/Kaunas/Klaipėda
policies.eligibility: Under 36, no home owned, first home in an eligible regional municipality, mortgage approved by a participating bank.
policies.url_label: Seimas — Law on the Financial Incentive for Young Families Acquiring a First Home (EN)
policies.caveat: Annual budget is capped (≈ €5.6m allocated in May 2026) and certificates go on a first-come basis, so applications open for a day and queue. Useless for a family that must stay in a big city for work.

policies.name: Free school and pre-primary meals, free child health cover
policies.what: All pre-primary pupils and pupils in grades 1–2 get free school meals regardless of income; older pupils only if family income is under €349.50/person. Children under 18 are covered by compulsory health insurance at state expense, with free GP, hospital and dental care in the public system, and textbooks are free.
policies.value: ≈ €40–60/month saved per child in pre-primary/grades 1–2 on meals; €0 for public health care
policies.eligibility: All children resident in Lithuania.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Social Security and Labour — free school meals
policies.caveat: Universal free meals stop after grade 2; the €148 school-supplies grant is means-tested and out of reach at median income.

official.label: Sodra — State Social Insurance Fund (English)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Lithuania

LU.note: For a two-earner family with small children Luxembourg is probably the most generous country in Europe: each parent can take up to 6 months of parental leave paid at close to full salary (max €4,619/month), crèche is free for 20 hours a week from age 1, child benefit is over €300 per child and school-age care, meals, books and all public transport are free. The weak point is housing: rents are among the highest in the EU and the rent subsidy is out of reach for a median two-earner household. Amounts are index-linked and rose in June 2026.

headline.cash: €630/month for 2 kids (allocation familiale €315.04 each, June 2026) + €1,740 birth grant
headline.leave: 20 weeks maternity at 100%; parental leave 4–6 months per parent at €2,771–€4,619/month; 10 days paternity
headline.childcare: 20 h/week free crèche ages 1–4 (46 weeks/year); income-capped fees beyond; free school-age care and lunch from 4
headline.tax: joint taxation (class 2) for married couples; child bonus folded into the family allowance

policies.name: Congé parental (paid parental leave, each parent)
policies.what: Each parent has an individual, non-transferable right per child: 4 or 6 months full-time, 8 or 12 months half-time, or split over up to 20 months. The CAE pays average earnings of the previous 12 months, between €2,771.33 and €4,618.88/month full-time (index June 2026). One parent starts right after maternity leave; the other before the child turns 6.
policies.value: ≈ €4,000–4,600/month for 6 months per parent at median pay, i.e. up to ≈ €50,000+ per child if both parents take full leave
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed, insured in Luxembourg for 12 continuous months before the leave, working at least 10 h/week.
policies.caveat: Part-time formulas need employer agreement; the second parent's leave is lost if not taken before age 6.

policies.name: Chèque-service accueil (CSA): 20 free hours + income-capped crèche fees
policies.what: Children aged 1–4 in an accredited crèche, mini-crèche or (from 2026) childminder get 20 hours/week free for 46 weeks/year regardless of income. Beyond that the State pays up to €7/hour (since Jan 2026), parents an income-graded share; meals capped near €4.50. The 2026 reform makes care fully free below 2× minimum wage and promises every child a place by 2030.
policies.value: ≈ €6,400/year per child in free hours (≈ €12,900 for 2 kids); a full-time crèche place then costs a median family roughly €300–600/month net
policies.eligibility: Resident children from 1 year until school entry (children of cross-border workers also eligible); parents must register for the CSA with their commune.
policies.caveat: Places are unevenly distributed regionally; parents who do not disclose income pay the maximum tariff; under-1s are not covered by the free hours.

policies.name: Allocation pour l'avenir des enfants (family allowance) + birth grant
policies.what: Universal monthly child benefit of €315.04 per child (index 992.24, from 1 June 2026), rising by €23.81 from age 6 and €59.44 from age 12, plus a back-to-school allowance from age 6. Birth grant of 3 × €580.03 (prenatal, birth, postnatal) tied to medical check-ups. Indexed to prices since 2021.
policies.value: €630/month (≈ €7,560/year) for 2 kids under 6, plus ≈ €1,740 per birth
policies.eligibility: Every child legally resident in Luxembourg (and children of cross-border workers); paid by the CAE, no income test.
policies.caveat: Single flat amount per child since 2016 (no higher rate for larger families); the former child tax bonus is already included in it.

policies.name: Congé de maternité + congé de paternité
policies.what: Maternity leave of 20 weeks (8 before, 12 after birth) paid by the CNS at 100% of the highest salary of the previous 3 months, capped at 5× the social minimum wage (≈ €13,800/month). Fathers or second parents get 10 paid days of paternity leave, the first 2 paid by the employer and the rest reimbursed by the State.
policies.value: ≈ 4.6 months of full salary per birth for the mother, 2 weeks for the father
policies.eligibility: Insured employees and self-employed with 6 months of affiliation in the year before the leave; dismissal protected.
policies.caveat: Followed directly by the first parent's parental leave if that option is chosen; no extension for breastfeeding beyond daily breaks.

policies.name: Free school-age care and lunches, free public transport, free schoolbooks
policies.what: Since September 2022 the maison relais (after-school care) and lunch are free during school weeks for all children in compulsory education (from age 4, précoce from 3), regardless of income. All public transport has been free nationwide since March 2020, including for children. Compulsory schoolbooks are free in secondary school.
policies.value: Roughly €300–500/month saved per school-age child on care and meals, plus zero transport costs for the whole family
policies.eligibility: All children attending school in Luxembourg; care requires CSA registration with the commune.
policies.url_label: MEN — Gratuité de l'accueil et des repas
policies.caveat: Free care applies to school weeks only; holiday care still carries an income-graded CSA fee.

official.label: Caisse pour l'avenir des enfants (CAE) — family benefits and parental leave

guide.label: EU Your Europe — Family benefits

LV.note: Latvia pays earnings-related leave at lower rates than its neighbours (80% maternity, then 60% or 43.75% parental benefit), but layers a flat child-care allowance on top, which jumped from €171 to €298/month in 2026, and a €600 birth grant. Municipal kindergarten is legally guaranteed from 18 months and tuition-free (parents pay meals); Riga currently reports no waiting list, though it is cutting co-funding of private places. The €250/month tax allowance per dependant is worth about €64 per child; a state mortgage guarantee for families with children is the only housing lever and requires a loan, not savings.

headline.cash: €298/month child-care allowance until 18 months + family state benefit (€25 for 1 child, €100 for 2) + €600 birth grant (2026)
headline.leave: maternity 112 days at 80%; parental benefit 60% until child is 1 (or 43.75% until 1.5), incl. 2 non-transferable months per parent; 10 days paternity at 80%
headline.childcare: municipal kindergarten place guaranteed from 18 months, tuition-free; meals ≈ €2.15/day in Riga after city co-funding
headline.tax: €250/month per child off taxable income (≈ €64/child/month at the 25.5% rate)

policies.name: Maternity, paternity and parental benefit (vecāku pabalsts)
policies.what: Maternity benefit: 112 days (56+56, up to 140) at 80% of insured earnings, no cap. Paternity: 10 working days at 80%. Parental benefit: 60% of average insured earnings until the child is 1 (13 months incl. 2 non-transferable months per parent) or 43.75% until 1.5 (19 months). Father's 2 months usable until age 8.
policies.value: ≈ €900/month at a €1,500 gross wage for 13 months (60% option) ≈ €11,700 per child, plus 80% during 112 maternity days
policies.eligibility: Employees/self-employed with contributions in 3 of the last 6 months or 6 of the last 24.
policies.caveat: Option cannot be changed once chosen. Working while on parental benefit reduces it to 75% in 2026. For births from 2026 only maternity-leave days count towards the parental benefit period.

policies.name: Child-care allowance (bērna kopšanas pabalsts) + family state benefit + birth grant
policies.what: Flat child-care allowance of €298/month for every child under 18 months (raised from €171 in 2026), then €42.69 to age 2, paid on top of parental benefit to the same parent. Family state benefit from age 1: €25/month for one child, €100 for two, €225 for three. One-off childbirth allowance €600 for births from 1 Jan 2026 (was €421.17).
policies.value: ≈ €325–400/month in the newborn's first year (€298 + €25–100) plus €600 at birth; €100/month once both kids are over 1
policies.eligibility: Permanent residents registered with the child; no income test.
policies.caveat: Payment for the 1.5–2 year band is being phased out for children born after 2 Nov 2026. Family state benefit only starts at the child's first birthday and is tiny for one child.

policies.name: Personal income tax allowance for dependants
policies.what: Each dependent child reduces the claiming parent's taxable income by €250/month (€3,000/year) on top of the fixed €550/month non-taxable minimum; PIT rate is 25.5% up to €105,300/year (2025–2026). Applied monthly by the employer via the electronic wage tax book.
policies.value: ≈ €127.50/month more net pay for 2 kids (≈ €1,530/year)
policies.eligibility: Any working parent registering the child as a dependant in the VID EDS system; only one parent per child.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Finance — non-taxable minimum and tax allowances
policies.caveat: Allowance frozen at €250 since 2021 despite inflation; worth nothing if the parent's income is already below the non-taxable minimum.

policies.name: Tuition-free municipal kindergarten from 18 months
policies.what: Education Law entitles every child from 1.5 years to a place in a municipal pre-school; tuition is free, parents pay only meals. In Riga three meals cost €4.30/day with the city paying half (€2.15) for Riga-registered children. If the municipality cannot offer a place it must co-finance a private kindergarten (Riga ~€300+/month).
policies.value: ≈ €45/month per child for meals in Riga; two kids in municipal kindergarten ≈ €90/month
policies.eligibility: Children registered in the municipality; co-financing only for Riga-declared children.
policies.url_label: Riga City — kindergarten and school meal support
policies.caveat: Riga says it has no waiting list in 2026 but plans to halve private-kindergarten co-funding where municipal places exist; smaller municipalities and Pierīga can still have shortages for 1.5–3 year olds.

policies.name: ALTUM state mortgage guarantee for families with children
policies.what: State guarantee replacing part of the down payment on a first-home loan: in Riga, Pierīga and Jūrmala 10% of the loan (max €10,000) with one child, 15% (max €15,000) with two; outside those areas 30–40%. Lets banks finance up to 95% of the property value on transactions up to €300,000; guarantee runs 10 years.
policies.value: Buy a €150,000 flat with ≈ €7,500 own savings instead of €22,500+ (2 kids, Riga)
policies.eligibility: Families with children up to 23 or expecting a baby, regular income but insufficient savings; needs a bank mortgage approval.
policies.url_label: ALTUM — housing guarantees for families with children
policies.caveat: It is a guarantee, not a grant: the family still repays the full loan and pays a guarantee fee. The 'Balsts' cash subsidy is only for families with 3+ children or a disabled child. No rent allowance exists at median income.

MT.note: Malta's stand-out policy for a dual-earner couple is the Free Childcare Scheme: full-time childcare from 3 months to 3 years at no cost for working parents, followed by free state kindergarten from 3. Cash support is modest at a median wage (about €1,090 per child per year plus a birth bonus) and paid parental leave beyond maternity is short and low-paid. Because most young Maltese buy rather than rent, the state leans on first-time-buyer help (10% deposit scheme, €1,000/yr grant, stamp-duty exemption) rather than rent subsidies, which are only for low incomes.

headline.cash: ≈ €2,180/yr for 2 kids above the €30,000 income threshold (Children's Allowance ≈ €450 + €640 supplement per child, 2026); €1,000/€1,500 birth bonus
headline.leave: 18 weeks maternity (14 at full pay, 4 at €213.54/wk) + 10 days paternity at full pay; parental leave 4 months each, only 2 paid at ~50% of sickness benefit
headline.childcare: Free Childcare Scheme 3 months–3 years for working parents (up to ~210 h/month); free state kindergarten from 3
headline.tax: parent rates 2026: first €18,500 tax-free with 2+ children (vs €12,000 single), 15% to €25,500, 25% to €60,000

policies.name: Free Childcare Scheme (3 months–3 years)
policies.what: Government pays fees at registered childcare centres for children aged 3 months to 3 years when both parents work (or study). Entitlement is 110% of one parent's monthly working hours plus 20 hours/month for commuting, i.e. about 210 hours/month for full-timers. Run by Jobsplus (new 4-year €276m contract, 2025). From age 3, state kindergarten is free.
policies.value: ≈ €400–600/month per child saved versus private fees (≈ €10,000–14,000/yr for two children)
policies.eligibility: Both parents (or a single parent) in employment paying social security, or in recognised education; child registered at a participating centre.
policies.caveat: Places at popular centres fill up early (register during pregnancy); hours beyond the entitlement, meals and extras are billed; eligibility ends the term the child turns 3.

policies.name: Parent income-tax rates (new 2026 bands)
policies.what: A parent who maintains a child under 18 (23 if in full-time education) is taxed at parent rates. Budget 2026 split these by family size: with 2+ children the first €18,500 is tax-free, 15% to €25,500, 25% to €60,000, 35% above (one child: €14,500 / €21,000). Single rates start taxing at €12,000. Married-rates version: €22,500 tax-free with 2+ children.
policies.value: roughly €1,000–1,500/yr less tax at a median wage compared with single rates (2026), on top of general 2025 band cuts
policies.eligibility: Resident parents with dependent children; chosen on the annual return (or via FSS on the payslip).
policies.url_label: Malta Tax & Customs Administration — New tax rates 2026 (PDF)
policies.caveat: Only one computation applies per return: a married couple either uses joint married rates or one spouse uses parent rates and the other single rates; the government has said the new bands are set for three years.

policies.name: Maternity leave, paternity leave and parental leave
policies.what: Maternity: 18 weeks, first 14 at full pay from the employer, last 4 paid by government at €213.54/week (2026); 6 weeks after birth compulsory. Paternity: 10 working days at full pay. Parental leave: 4 months per parent per child until age 8; 2 months non-transferable, paid at 50% of the sickness-benefit rate for under-4s (about €80–95/week), the rest unpaid.
policies.value: ≈ 3.5 months of full pay for the mother + 2 weeks for the father per birth; paid parental leave adds only ≈ €700–800 per parent
policies.eligibility: All employees (parental leave after 12 months' service); self-employed mothers get a flat maternity benefit instead.
policies.url_label: DIER — Maternity leave (Department of Industrial and Employment Relations)
policies.caveat: Beyond 14 weeks the mother's income drops to roughly the minimum wage, and shared parental leave is close to unpaid, so most families rely on the free childcare scheme from month 4–5.

policies.name: Children's Allowance + Children's Allowance Supplement + Child Birth Bonus
policies.what: Means-tested Children's Allowance: at household income above €30,000 (2026 threshold, up from €27,434) a flat minimum of €8.66/week ≈ €450/yr per child; up to €27.29/week (≈ €1,419/yr) at very low incomes. Since 2025 a supplement adds €640/yr per child above the threshold (€910 below), paid quarterly. One-off birth bonus (2026): €1,000 first child, €1,500 second, €2,000 third+.
policies.value: ≈ €2,180/yr (≈ €180/month) for two children at two median wages, plus €2,500 in birth bonuses for a first and second child
policies.eligibility: Parents resident in Malta with children under 16 (21 if in education/registering unemployed); automatic yearly means test.
policies.url_label: Social Security Malta — Children's Allowance (income exceeds threshold)
policies.caveat: Two full-time earners almost always exceed the €30,000 threshold, so they get the flat minimum; the In-Work Benefit for couples stops at about €36,850 combined income.

policies.name: 10% Deposit Scheme + First-Time Buyer grant and stamp-duty exemption
policies.what: Housing Authority arranges a bank loan for the 10% deposit on a first home worth up to €250,000 (Budget 2026) for buyers aged 21–39 who qualify for a mortgage but lack savings; the Authority pays the interest, so only capital is repaid over 25 years. First-time buyers also get €1,000/yr for 10 years and pay no stamp duty below €200,000.
policies.value: ≈ €25,000 deposit financed interest-free + €10,000 grant + up to €7,000 duty saved; rent subsidies exist only for low incomes
policies.eligibility: First-time buyers resident in Malta, 21–39 for the deposit scheme, property ≤ €250,000, bank loan approval.
policies.caveat: €250,000 buys little near Valletta/Sliema, so the scheme mainly helps in cheaper localities or Gozo; a two-median-income couple still needs a mortgage of ~€225,000, roughly 5× joint income.

NL.note: For a two-earner family the Netherlands works through one big lever: the kinderopvangtoeslag, which refunds 79-92% of daycare costs even at a household income of about €90,000, provided both parents work. Everything else is modest: child benefit of about €200/month for two kids, an income-tested kindgebonden budget that is mostly phased out at two median wages, and leave beyond the mother's 16 weeks paid at only 70%. Housing benefit is out of reach at this income, daycare places have waiting lists, and many providers charge above the subsidised hourly rate, so the parents' own share is often higher than the tables suggest.

headline.cash: ≈ €199/month for 2 kids under 6 (kinderbijslag €298.40/quarter each, from July 2026) + kindgebonden budget ≈ €0-2,500/yr depending on hours
headline.leave: 16 weeks maternity at 100%; partner 1 week 100% + 5 weeks 70%; 9 weeks per parent at 70% in year 1
headline.childcare: kinderopvangtoeslag covers 78.9% (1st child) and 92.2% (2nd) of €11.23/hour at ≈ €90k household income (2026)
headline.tax: IACK up to €3,032/yr for the lower earner, but only if a child was born before 2025

policies.name: Kinderopvangtoeslag (childcare benefit)
policies.what: Monthly refund of daycare costs for working parents, paid by Dienst Toeslagen. In 2026 it covers up to €11.23/hour (daycare) for max 230 hours/child/month; 96% at household income up to €56,413, still 78.9% for the 1st and 92.2% for the 2nd child at about €90,000, and never below 36.5%/68.2%. Parents pay only the remainder.
policies.value: ≈ €2,700/month subsidy for 2 kids in daycare 3 days/week at two median wages; parents pay ≈ €450-600/month
policies.eligibility: Both parents (or single parent) working or studying; hours capped at 140% of the lower earner's working hours; child in a registered provider.
policies.caveat: Many providers charge €12-13/hour, above the €11.23 subsidised rate, and urban waiting lists run 6-12 months. It is an advance based on estimated income, so over-payments are clawed back. A near-free (96% for all incomes) system has been announced but postponed; the government's stated target is 2029.

policies.name: Zwangerschapsverlof, geboorteverlof and betaald ouderschapsverlof
policies.what: Mother: 16 weeks maternity leave at 100% of pay (UWV, capped at the maximum daily wage, above a median salary). Partner: 1 week at full pay from the employer plus 5 weeks at 70% (UWV) within 6 months. Both parents: 9 weeks paid parental leave at 70% of daily wage (capped) in the first year, plus 17 unpaid weeks each.
policies.value: ≈ 16 weeks full pay + 6 weeks partner + 2 x 9 weeks at 70% per child for a median-wage couple
policies.eligibility: Employees; self-employed mothers get a separate ZEZ benefit. Employer applies to UWV.
policies.caveat: Paid parental leave must be used in the first year and is only 70%; the remaining 17 weeks per parent are unpaid unless a collective agreement tops up.

policies.name: Kinderbijslag (child benefit) + kindgebonden budget
policies.what: Kinderbijslag: universal, paid quarterly by SVB, €298.40 per child aged 0-5 from July 2026 (€362.35 at 6-11), no income test. Kindgebonden budget: income-tested top-up of up to about €2,580 per child under 12 (2026), reduced by 7.6% of household income above €39,141 for couples, so largely gone at two full-time median wages but ≈ €2,400/yr if one parent works part-time.
policies.value: ≈ €199/month for 2 small kids from kinderbijslag; kindgebonden budget ≈ €0-2,500/yr depending on hours worked
policies.eligibility: All residents with children (kinderbijslag); kindgebonden budget also has an asset limit for couples.
policies.caveat: Kinderbijslag is paid in arrears per quarter and is small by EU standards; the kindgebonden budget's phase-out rate was raised to 7.6% in 2026.

policies.name: Inkomensafhankelijke combinatiekorting (IACK)
policies.what: Tax credit for the lower-earning working parent of a child under 12: 11.45% of earnings above €6,239, up to €3,032 (2026). It has been abolished for children born on or after 1 January 2025; families whose youngest qualifying child was born before 2025 keep it, with the maximum cut in 9 annual steps from 2027.
policies.value: up to ≈ €3,000/year for the lower earner, but only if the toddler was born before 2025; nothing for the newborn
policies.eligibility: Working parent earning above €6,239 with a co-resident child under 12 born before 2025, earning less than the partner.
policies.caveat: Being phased out: new parents get nothing, and existing recipients lose it stepwise 2027-2035. There is no family splitting or child tax credit otherwise.

NO.note: For a working couple Norway is among the most generous in Europe: 49 weeks of leave at 100% pay (up to 6G ≈ 819,000 kr, i.e. full replacement at median wage), a legal right to a barnehage place from age 1 at a capped 1,200 kr/month, and 20 paid sick-child days a year. The child benefit is modest and was flattened to one rate in Feb 2026; the housing allowance (bostøtte) is not reachable at median income, rents in Oslo are high and there is no family taxation. The main practical catch is the gap for children born in December who wait until August for a place.

headline.cash: 4,024 kr/month (≈ €345) tax-free barnetrygd for 2 children (2,012 kr each from 1 Feb 2026)
headline.leave: 49 weeks at 100% (15 mother + 15 father quota + 16 shared) or 61 weeks at 80%; income covered up to 6G = 819,294 kr; + 10 paid sick-child days per parent per year
headline.childcare: legal right to a place from age 1; max 1,200 kr/month (700 kr in rural municipalities), 30% off 2nd child, free from 3rd
headline.tax: foreldrefradrag: childcare costs deductible up to 25,000 kr + 15,000 kr per extra child (≈ 8,800 kr tax saved)

policies.name: Barnehage with makspris (national fee cap)
policies.what: Children have a legal right to a barnehage place from the month they turn 1 (if born Aug–Nov; otherwise from August). Parent fee is capped nationally at 1,200 kr/month since 1 Aug 2025 (700 kr in 189 least-central municipalities, free in Finnmark/Nord-Troms), plus food money; 2nd child gets ≥30% off, 3rd is free; nobody pays more than 6% of household income; 20 h/week free for 2–5-year-olds if income < 692,465 kr (from Aug 2026).
policies.value: ≈ 2,040 kr/month (≈ €175) + food money for two full-time places; the public subsidy is ≈ 18,000–20,000 kr per place per month
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the municipality, from age 1; apply by 1 March for August intake.
policies.caveat: A child born in December waits until the next August; kontantstøtte (7,500 kr/month, months 13–19, 5 years' NI membership required) partly bridges this. Childcare costs are also deductible (foreldrefradrag, up to 25,000 + 15,000 kr/year).

policies.name: Foreldrepenger (parental benefit)
policies.what: Paid leave of 49 weeks at 100% of income or 61 weeks at 80%: 3 weeks before birth, a 15-week mother's quota, a 15-week father's quota (19 + 19 at 80%) and 16 shared weeks. Income replaced up to 6G = 819,294 kr/year (May 2026); most employers pay the excess. Based on the last 3 months' pay. Father also gets 2 weeks at birth (paid under most agreements).
policies.value: 100% of a ≈ 52,000 kr median monthly wage for 49 weeks shared (≈ 11 months), no cap bites at median wage
policies.eligibility: Worked with income in 6 of the last 10 months before leave; otherwise a one-off engangsstønad (≈ 92,000 kr, 2025).
policies.caveat: Quota weeks unused by one parent are lost; the 100%/80% choice cannot be changed later.

policies.name: Barnetrygd (child benefit)
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, monthly, automatic from birth to 18: 2,012 kr per child from 1 Feb 2026, now one flat rate for all ages (the previous higher under-6 rate and lower 6–18 rate were merged). Extra 512 kr in Finnmark/Svalbard; single parents get an extended benefit.
policies.value: 4,024 kr/month (≈ €345) for two children
policies.eligibility: Children resident in Norway; automatic for children born in Norway.

policies.name: Omsorgsdager / omsorgspenger (sick-child days)
policies.what: Each parent can stay home with full pay when a child under 12 is ill or the childminder is sick: 10 days per parent per year with 1–2 children (15 days with 3+; doubled for single parents), paid by the employer at ordinary salary up to 6G. Self-certification for the first 3 days.
policies.value: 20 paid days per year for the couple (≈ 1 month of salary protected)
policies.eligibility: Employees after 4 weeks in the job; self-employed from day 11.

policies.name: Free child healthcare, helsestasjon and public dental care
policies.what: Children under 16 pay no user fee (egenandel) at the GP, emergency room or hospital; the municipal helsestasjon provides free check-ups, home visit after birth and vaccinations to age 5; the public dental service treats children and young people free until 18 (reduced fee 19–24). School is free and 12 h/week of after-school SFO is free for 1st–2nd graders.
policies.value: ≈ 0 kr out of pocket for child health, dental and preventive care
policies.eligibility: All residents registered in the National Insurance Scheme.
policies.caveat: GP (fastlege) shortages in some municipalities; adults pay egenandel and full dental cost.

PL.note: Poland now front-loads cash on small children: universal 800+ plus the 2024 'Aktywny Rodzic' payment of 1,500 zł a month for every child aged 12–35 months make a two-toddler household one of the best-supported in the EU in pure cash terms. Paid leave is long (61 weeks, 81.5%) but the father's own 9 weeks are only 70%. Weak spots: nursery (żłobek) places for under-3s are still scarce outside big cities, and there is no housing support reachable at a median wage (the 2% first-home loan scheme closed in 2023; dodatek mieszkaniowy is for low incomes only).

headline.cash: 1,600 zł/month (≈ €375) for 2 kids from 800+, plus 1,500 zł/month (≈ €350) per child aged 1–3 via Aktywny Rodzic
headline.leave: 20 weeks maternity + 41 weeks parental, 81.5% pay; 9 weeks reserved for the father at 70%; 2 weeks paternity at 100%
headline.childcare: public preschool from age 3: guaranteed place, 5 hours/day free; nursery fee covered up to 1,500 zł/month for ages 1–3
headline.tax: child tax credit 1,112 zł/year per child (≈ €520/year for 2), refundable; joint filing for spouses

policies.name: Aktywny Rodzic (Active Parent) — 1,500 zł/month for children aged 12–35 months
policies.what: Since October 2024, for each child aged 12–35 months parents choose one of: 'Aktywni rodzice w pracy' 1,500 zł/month paid to working parents; 'Aktywnie w żłobku' up to 1,500 zł/month paid straight to the nursery/childminder (not above the actual fee); or 'Aktywnie w domu' 500 zł/month if the child stays home. No income ceiling.
policies.value: 1,500 zł/month (≈ €350) per child for 24 months — up to 36,000 zł per child; two toddlers can both qualify
policies.eligibility: Residents with a child aged 12–35 months. The 1,500 zł work variant requires both parents (or the sole parent) to be professionally active, roughly: social-insurance contributions from at least half the minimum wage each; the nursery variant only needs a place in a registered żłobek/klub/childminder.
policies.caveat: Replaced the old Rodzinny Kapitał Opiekuńczy (12,000 zł per second child) — households with only one child now get more than before. Nursery places remain scarce in many gminy, so the 1,500 zł 'in żłobek' option is often not usable in practice.

policies.name: Rodzina 800+ (świadczenie wychowawcze)
policies.what: Universal child benefit of 800 zł per month for every child until age 18 (raised from 500 zł in January 2024). No income test, paid by ZUS; benefit year runs June–May, application online each year.
policies.value: 1,600 zł/month (≈ €375) for 2 children, tax-free, on top of Aktywny Rodzic
policies.eligibility: All parents resident in Poland with children under 18; no income or work condition.
policies.caveat: Flat amount, not indexed — its real value erodes with inflation; the 2024 increase was the first since 2016.

policies.name: Paid maternity + parental leave (zasiłek macierzyński)
policies.what: 20 weeks maternity leave, then 41 weeks parental leave shared between parents, of which 9 weeks are non-transferable for each parent (since 2023). Benefit is 81.5% of pay for the whole 52 weeks (mother's share) if requested within 21 days of birth, otherwise 100% then 70%; the father's 9 reserved weeks are paid at 70%. Plus 2 weeks paternity leave at 100%.
policies.value: ≈ 5,100 zł/month (≈ €1,200) for about 12 months at a median wage (~7,300 zł gross), plus 9 weeks for the father at ~4,400 zł
policies.eligibility: Employees and other persons covered by sickness insurance (also self-employed paying contributions); no waiting period for employees.
policies.caveat: No cap for employees, but the 81.5% option must be requested in the first 21 days; the father's 9 weeks are lost if he does not take them.

policies.name: Ulga na dziecko (child tax credit) + joint spousal filing
policies.what: Annual income-tax credit of 1,112.04 zł for the first and second child each (2,000.04 zł third, 2,700 zł fourth+), deducted from PIT; any unused part is refunded up to the social/health contributions paid. With two or more children there is no income limit (112,000 zł joint limit applies only to one-child families). Spouses may also file jointly.
policies.value: 2,224 zł/year (≈ €520) for 2 children at a median wage; joint filing adds a further saving if one parent goes part-time
policies.eligibility: Parents taxed on the progressive scale (12%/32%); 2+ children: no income test.
policies.caveat: Amounts have been frozen since 2007 and are small relative to 800+; refund is limited to contributions actually paid.

policies.name: Public preschool (przedszkole) from age 3 — guaranteed place, 5 free hours
policies.what: Every child aged 3–6 has a legal right to a place in a public preschool run by its gmina; at least 5 hours a day are free, and each extra hour is capped by law (about 1.4 zł in 2025/26). Parents pay only for meals. The last year (age 6) is compulsory and free. Primary-school textbooks are free; child healthcare is free under NFZ.
policies.value: Full-day public preschool for roughly 150 zł/month in fees plus ~200–300 zł meals per child (≈ €80–110), vs 1,500–2,500 zł privately
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the gmina from the school year they turn 3 (2.5-year-olds if places allow).
policies.url_label: gov.pl / MEN — public preschool is free
policies.caveat: The guarantee starts at 3; for under-3s public żłobek coverage is still only around a third of children nationally and much lower in rural gminy.

PT.note: For a young two-earner couple Portugal's big three are free crèche for every child born since Sept 2021 (Creche Feliz), the IRS Jovem tax exemption for workers up to 35, and solid parental leave paid at 100% (or 80–90% for longer options). Cash child benefit (abono de família) is income-tested and small at a median wage, and public pré-escolar is free from age 3. The catch is capacity: crèche and Porta 65 rent support are both rationed by places and rounds, and rents in Lisbon/Porto outrun any subsidy.

headline.cash: abono de família ≈ €90–220/month for 2 kids under 3 at a median household income (2026), falling after age 3
headline.leave: 120 days at 100% or 150 at 80% (150 at 100% / 180 at 83–90% if shared) + 28 days father-only at 100%
headline.childcare: Creche Feliz: free crèche 0–3 for all children born from 1 Sep 2021 (state pays €551.50/month); free public pré-escolar from 3
headline.tax: IRS Jovem: 100% income-tax exemption in year 1, 75% years 2–4, 50% years 5–7, 25% years 8–10, up to age 35 (cap €29,542/yr)

policies.name: Creche Feliz — rede de creches gratuitas (free crèche 0–3)
policies.what: Every child born on or after 1 Sept 2021 gets a free place, regardless of family income, in crèches of the social/solidarity sector, licensed childminders and public or affiliated private crèches. The state pays the full base fee (€551.50/month in 2026) directly to the crèche. Fully phased in for all three crèche years since 2024/25.
policies.value: ≈ €550/month per child (≈ €13,000/yr for two children) versus paying privately
policies.eligibility: Children under 3 born from 1 Sept 2021; place must be requested online via Segurança Social Direta.
policies.url_label: Segurança Social — Creche Feliz, rede de creches gratuitas
policies.caveat: Free only where a place exists: waiting lists remain long in Lisbon, Porto and the Algarve, and non-affiliated private crèches are not covered. Meals/extended hours may still be charged.

policies.name: Licença parental inicial + licença parental exclusiva do pai
policies.what: Initial parental leave: 120 days at 100% of reference pay or 150 days at 80%; if the father takes at least 30 days alone, 150 days at 100% or 180 days at 83% (a 90% option for an equal split since 2023). Father: 28 days exclusive leave at 100% (7 right after birth) plus 7 optional; mother: 6 compulsory weeks.
policies.value: ≈ 5–6 months of full household pay replaced per birth, with no salary cap on the Social Security benefit
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed with 6 months of contributions; benefit paid by Segurança Social, tax-exempt.
policies.caveat: The additional 'licença parental alargada' (3 months per parent) is paid at only 25%. A citizens' bill for 180 days at 100% passed first reading in Jan 2026 but was not yet law in Sept 2026.

policies.name: IRS Jovem (young workers' income-tax exemption, 2025 model)
policies.what: Workers aged up to 35 pay reduced IRS on employment/self-employment income for 10 years: 100% exempt in year 1, 75% in years 2–4, 50% in years 5–7, 25% in years 8–10, on income up to 55× IAS (€29,542 in 2026). No degree required since 2025. Added to the standard child deduction of €600 per dependant (≈ €726–900 for under-3s).
policies.value: roughly €1,500–2,500/yr less tax per parent at a median wage in the 75% years; up to ≈ €5,000/yr for the household
policies.eligibility: Ages 18–35, not a dependant on someone else's return; opted in on the annual Modelo 3 (automatic proposal since 2026).
policies.url_label: Portal das Finanças — IRS Jovem FAQ
policies.caveat: Years used under the old (2020–24) regime count toward the 10; the benefit ends at 35 whatever remains.

policies.name: Abono de família para crianças e jovens
policies.what: Monthly child benefit by household reference income (annual income ÷ children+1). 2026 rates for a child under 3: €190.98 (1st bracket), €161.65 (2nd), €132.07 (3rd), €88.43 (4th); 4th bracket ends at €18,800 reference income. Children over 3 get €44.77–75.13; over 6 nothing in the 4th bracket. Extra for a second child under 3 (€39–65).
policies.value: roughly €90–220/month for a newborn + toddler (3rd–4th bracket at two median wages), dropping to ≈ €90 or less once both are over 3
policies.eligibility: Residents with children; reference income below ≈ €18,800/yr (2026); needs a yearly income re-check.
policies.caveat: Two full-time median earners sit near the top bracket and can lose the benefit entirely for children over 6; a birth grant (abono pré-natal) is paid only from the 13th week of pregnancy at the same bracket rates.

policies.name: Porta 65 Jovem (rent subsidy for under-35s)
policies.what: Pays a share of the rent to tenants aged 18–35 (one partner may be up to 37) for 12 months, renewable up to 5 years; average award ≈ €275/month in 2026. Household gross income must be below 4× the minimum wage (≈ €3,680/month in 2026) and rent below a municipal ceiling. Rolling online rounds on Portal da Habitação.
policies.value: ≈ €275/month (≈ €3,300/yr) if selected; two median earners with kids qualify on income
policies.eligibility: 18–35, renting a permanent home with a registered contract, no owned housing, income under the cap.
policies.caveat: Rounds are oversubscribed and ranked by lowest income, so median earners often miss out; rent ceilings are below market in Lisbon/Porto. Under-35 first-time buyers separately get IMT/stamp-duty exemption and a state mortgage guarantee, but only if they can afford the loan.

official.label: Segurança Social — family and parenthood benefits

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Portugal

RO.note: Romania's real strength for a two-earner family is time: an earnings-related child-raising benefit (85% of net pay) until the child is 2, on top of 126 days of maternity leave, and a cash bonus if a parent goes back to work early. Cash allowances are universal but have been frozen for two years (2025-2026) under austerity, a 10% health contribution has been taken from the child-raising benefit since Aug 2025, and there is no child tax relief at a median wage. Public kindergarten is free from age 3, but public creche places for under-3s are scarce and housing support is essentially absent.

headline.cash: ≈ 1,011 lei (≈ €200)/month for a newborn + toddler (alocația de stat, frozen 2025-2026)
headline.leave: 126 days maternity at 85% + child-raising leave to age 2 at 85% of net pay (min 1,651 / max 8,500 lei), 2 months reserved for the other parent; 10-15 days paternity
headline.childcare: public kindergarten free from age 3 (compulsory from 4); public creche free except meals (~13-22 lei/day) but places scarce
headline.tax: none reachable at median wage (personal deduction only up to ~6,050 lei gross)

policies.name: Indemnizația pentru creșterea copilului (child-raising leave and benefit)
policies.what: Either parent can stay home until the child turns 2 and receive 85% of their average net income of the previous 12 months, minimum 1,651 lei and maximum 8,500 lei gross per month (2026). At least 2 months are reserved for the other parent or are lost. Since 1 Aug 2025 a 10% health contribution (CASS) is deducted.
policies.value: ≈ 3,600-3,700 lei (≈ €710-730)/month net for up to 24 months per child for a parent on a median net wage of roughly 4,800 lei
policies.eligibility: 12 months of taxable income in the 2 years before the birth; one parent at a time; either parent.
policies.url_label: ANPIS (National Agency for Payments and Social Inspection) — Indemnizație creștere copil
policies.caveat: The 10% CASS deduction introduced by Law 141/2025 cuts the benefit by a tenth (max falls from 8,500 to 7,650 lei net). Payment starts only after the file is processed (often 1-3 months of delay).

policies.name: Alocația de stat pentru copii (universal child allowance)
policies.what: Monthly benefit for every child resident in Romania, no income test: 719 lei for children under 2 (under 3 if disabled) and 292 lei from age 2 to 18 (2026). The law provides automatic inflation indexation, but it was suspended for 2025 (OUG 156/2024) and again for 2026 (Law 141/2025).
policies.value: ≈ 1,011 lei (≈ €200)/month for a newborn (719) plus a 3-year-old (292)
policies.eligibility: All children legally resident in Romania; paid to the parent from the month after the application.
policies.url_label: ANPIS Bucharest — Alocație de stat pentru copii
policies.caveat: Frozen at Dec 2024 level for two consecutive years; real value has fallen roughly 10% with inflation. Drops from 719 to 292 lei on the child's 2nd birthday.

policies.name: Stimulentul de inserție (return-to-work bonus)
policies.what: A parent entitled to child-raising leave who instead earns taxable income gets a monthly bonus until the child is 2: 1,500 lei/month if they return before the child is 6 months old, 650 lei/month if they return later (2026). Paid on top of the salary; the other parent's leave months are not affected.
policies.value: 1,500 lei (≈ €295)/month for up to ~18 months if the second earner goes back before the baby is 6 months old; otherwise 650 lei (≈ €127)/month
policies.eligibility: Same 12-months-of-income condition as the child-raising benefit; must earn taxable income while receiving it.
policies.caveat: Cannot be combined with the child-raising benefit for the same parent; amounts are not indexed.

policies.name: Concediu de maternitate + concediu paternal (maternity and paternity leave)
policies.what: Mothers get 126 calendar days of maternity leave (63 before + 63 after birth, minimum 42 days after birth) paid at 85% of the average income of the last 6 months from the health-insurance fund (CNAS), not the employer. Fathers get 10 working days of paid paternity leave, 15 days if they complete an infant-care course.
policies.value: ≈ 4 months at 85% of the mother's pay (≈ 4,100 lei ≈ €800/month at a 4,800 lei net wage) + 2-3 weeks fully paid for the father
policies.eligibility: Mother insured in the health system for at least 6 months in the last 12; father must be an employee.
policies.url_label: CNAS (National Health Insurance House) — maternity benefit payer
policies.caveat: The 85% is computed on income capped at 12 gross minimum wages; the maternity leave overlaps with the start of the child-raising leave rather than adding to it.

policies.name: Free public kindergarten from 3 and public creches; creche vouchers
policies.what: Public kindergarten (grădiniță) is free from age 3 and compulsory from age 4 (since 2023); parents of children in the extended day pay only a meal contribution of roughly 13-22 lei/day. Public creches (creșă, from 6 months) work the same way. Employers may give tax-free creche vouchers (up to 710 lei/month since Oct 2025) or reimburse creche/kindergarten fees up to 1,500 lei/month tax-free.
policies.value: ≈ 0 lei tuition for the 3-year-old; ~300-450 lei (≈ €60-90)/month for meals in a full-day public group
policies.eligibility: All resident children; enrolment via the national online platform each spring; priority to compulsory ages 4-5.
policies.caveat: Public creche capacity covers only a small share of under-3s, especially in Bucharest and big cities; private creches cost 2,000-4,000 lei/month. Creche vouchers exist only if the employer chooses to grant them and not while a parent is on child-raising leave.

official.label: ANPIS — family benefits agency (site frequently returns 503 to non-Romanian traffic)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Romania

SE.note: Sweden's package for a two-earner couple with small children rests on long, well-paid parental leave (480 days per child, ~80% of wage), near-free förskola under the maxtaxa (cut again from July 2026) and generous paid sick-child days. The universal child benefit has been frozen at 1,250 kr since 2018 and the housing allowance is unreachable at two median wages; Sweden has no family taxation. The real weak spot for renters is the housing market itself: first-hand rental queues in Stockholm and Gothenburg run many years.

headline.cash: 2,650 kr/month (≈ €240) tax-free barnbidrag + flerbarnstillägg for 2 children (frozen since 2018)
headline.leave: 480 days per child, 390 at ~80% of wage (max 1,259 kr/day 2026), 90 days reserved per parent; + 120 sick-child days/child/year at ~80%
headline.childcare: place guaranteed from age 1; max 1,547 kr/month child 1 + 1,031 kr child 2 from 1 July 2026, meals included; 15 h/week free from age 3
headline.tax: none: individual taxation, no child tax credit

policies.name: Föräldrapenning (parental benefit)
policies.what: 480 days per child: 390 days at just under 80% of income (SGI), capped at 1,259 kr/day in 2026 (income ceiling 592,000 kr/year), plus 90 days at 180 kr/day. 90 days are reserved for each parent; up to 45 days can be handed to e.g. a grandparent (since July 2024). Usable until the child turns 12; 60 'double days' allowed before 15 months. Other parent also gets 10 paid days at birth.
policies.value: ≈ 29,000 kr/month (≈ €2,650) before tax at a 38,000 kr median wage, for ≈ 13 months at the high rate per child; many employers add föräldralön to ~90%
policies.eligibility: Insured in Sweden; income-based rate needs 240 days of SGI before birth, otherwise 250 kr/day basic level.
policies.caveat: Only 96 days can be saved past age 4; the 180 kr lowest-level days are close to worthless.

policies.name: Förskola under the maxtaxa (fee cap)
policies.what: Municipalities must offer a förskola place within 4 months of application from age 1, typically full-day with meals. Fees are capped nationally: from 1 July 2026 the first 10,000 kr of monthly household income is exempt, then 3% for child 1 (max 1,547 kr), 2% for child 2 (max 1,031 kr), 1% for child 3 (max 516 kr), ceiling income 61,560 kr/month. From the autumn the child turns 3, 15 h/week are free.
policies.value: ≈ 2,580 kr/month (≈ €235) for two full-time places incl. meals at two median wages (≈ 3,080 kr before July 2026)
policies.eligibility: All children from age 1 whose parents work, study, are on parental leave (limited hours) or unemployed.
policies.url_label: Stockholm stad — förskola fees 2026 (national maxtaxa rates)
policies.caveat: Place may be offered anywhere in the municipality; queues for specific popular förskolor; some big cities have staffing shortages.

policies.name: Tillfällig föräldrapenning / VAB (care of sick child)
policies.what: When a child under 12 is ill, either parent can stay home and claim VAB: up to 120 days per child per year at just under 80% of income (income cap 444,000 kr/year in 2026, i.e. roughly 940 kr/day max). Claimed online the same day; no doctor's note for the first 7 days.
policies.value: ≈ 900 kr/day (≈ €80) per sick day; a family with two toddlers in förskola typically uses 15–25 days a year (≈ 15,000–22,000 kr)
policies.eligibility: Working parents (or others caring for the child) with SGI in Sweden.
policies.url_label: Försäkringskassan — Care of a sick child (VAB)

policies.name: Barnbidrag + flerbarnstillägg (child benefit)
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, paid monthly and split between parents: 1,250 kr per child under 16 plus a large-family supplement of 150 kr for the second child (730 kr for three). Automatic, no application. The 1,250 kr rate has not been raised since March 2018.
policies.value: 2,650 kr/month (≈ €240) for two children
policies.eligibility: All children resident and insured in Sweden.
policies.caveat: Frozen in nominal terms since 2018, so its real value has fallen by roughly a quarter.

policies.name: Free child healthcare, BVC and dental care
policies.what: Children pay no fee for outpatient care in most regions (usually to age 18–20), prescription medicines are free under 18, and the child health centre (BVC) provides free check-ups, vaccinations and home visits. Dental care is free through the year the person turns 19 (lowered from 23 on 1 Jan 2025). School meals are free from förskoleklass.
policies.value: ≈ 0 kr out of pocket for child health and dental
policies.eligibility: All children registered in a region.
policies.caveat: Age limits for free care differ by region; the free-dental age was cut from 23 to 19 in 2025.
